item.title: Where is it going wrong for Carrick's Man Utd?
item.description: Thursday marks five months exactly since Man Utd announced Michael Carrick would be staying on as head coach. There will be little mood for celebrating anniversaries the morning after his worst night in the role.

item.title: Kylian Mbappe makes feelings clear on Barcelona clash after Real Madrid win
item.description: Kylian Mbappe makes feelings clear on Barcelona clash after Real Madrid win Real Madrid made it three wins from three games as they defeated RB Leipzig in their latest UEFA Champions League game at the Santiago Bernabeu last night. With this win, the Merengues have climbed to the fourth position on the League Phase table. While Los Blancos maintained their winning run, the forward Kylian Mbappe also kept up his scoring run in the competition. After scoring in the games against Inter Milan and AS Roma, he again got on the scoresheet, as he scored a beautiful goal to take the scoreline to 3-0 in favor of his team. As MARCA has reported, the Frenchman also spoke to the media after the match. The Real Madrid star highlighted how important this win can be for his team: “Every point is important for finishing in the top eight, and this is an important victory.” When asked if he was feeling confident about facing Barcelona, Mbappe assured that he was focused on the last night’s game: “We’ve only been thinking about Leipzig.” The forward wanted to continue pleasing the fans with his performances: “The Bernabéu wants us to score goals and play attacking football, and we want to please the fans. We try to bring them joy. ” Meanwhile, he was also looking to help his team win with these goals: “I’m fine. I have to score goals, help the team and make sure we win.” The Frenchman also had some words of encouragement for Vinicius Junior, who was visibly sad after another underwhelming performance: “If he’s sad, it’s because it means he wants to give a lot to the team and the fans. He should be proud of who he is.” Going forward, Kylian Mbappe will be facing an FC Barcelona side against whom he has particularly enjoyed scoring. Hopefully, he will be able to add a few goals in this Sunday’s El Clasico, and will be able to help his team get a win against the Blaugranes.

item.title: Bruno Fernandes turning on Michael Carrick exposes Man United’s unavoidable truth
item.description: Great, now the parents are arguing. It was pretty clear when Bruno Fernandes was hauled off in the 65th minute with Manchester United being thumped by Como in the Champions League that he was far from happy. He had spent his evening attempting to lead the United press, forlornly chasing after the ball like a terrier who had been tasked with closing down a flock of pigeons in a vast town square. Fernandes, like his United team-mates, got nowhere near it and Como toyed with them. Before his substitution for Joshua Zirkzee, a further white flag on a horrid evening for United, the captain had also wasted his energy by performatively flapping his arms, looking over his shoulder with the exasperated expression of ‘what are you guys doing back there?’ He trudged around the side of the pitch and returned to the bench without acknowledging his manager. And look, Fernandes is not exactly meant to be alright to be once again caught at the scene of a chastening night for United, their joint-heaviest defeat in the Champions League or something like that. But nor did we expect Fernandes to come out so strongly in his criticism at full-time . “It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," Fernandes said. Asked whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes replied: “That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes questioned his manager’s tactics after the heavy defeat to Como (PA Wire) Carrick appeared bemused, but there was an end-of-days look to United’s defeat and an end-of-days feel to the way Carrick put on a brave face and marched over the remaining United fans in Como to apologise at full-time. It was a gesture that, as the cycle of the United circus continues to spin, had striking similarities to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer holding his hands up to the United fans just days before he was sacked following the 4-1 defeat at Watford five years ago . A proud and respected former player left hurting by the decline at Old Trafford? It’s happening again, and everyone appears to have accepted Carrick’s days are numbered. Perhaps the surest sign of that is not just Fernandes rounding on his manager but Carrick actually saying something interesting in his response when asked about his captain’s comments. “There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren’t going to win,” replied said, pointedly. item.content:encoded: Great, now the parents are arguing. It was pretty clear when Bruno Fernandes was hauled off in the 65th minute with Manchester United being thumped by Como in the Champions League that he was far from happy. He had spent his evening attempting to lead the United press, forlornly chasing after the ball like a terrier who had been tasked with closing down a flock of pigeons in a vast town square. Fernandes, like his United team-mates, got nowhere near it and Como toyed with them. Before his substitution for Joshua Zirkzee, a further white flag on a horrid evening for United, the captain had also wasted his energy by performatively flapping his arms, looking over his shoulder with the exasperated expression of ‘what are you guys doing back there?’ He trudged around the side of the pitch and returned to the bench without acknowledging his manager. And look, Fernandes is not exactly meant to be alright to be once again caught at the scene of a chastening night for United, their joint-heaviest defeat in the Champions League or something like that. But nor did we expect Fernandes to come out so strongly in his criticism at full-time . “It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," Fernandes said. Asked whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes replied: “That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes questioned his manager’s tactics after the heavy defeat to Como (PA Wire) Carrick appeared bemused, but there was an end-of-days look to United’s defeat and an end-of-days feel to the way Carrick put on a brave face and marched over the remaining United fans in Como to apologise at full-time. It was a gesture that, as the cycle of the United circus continues to spin, had striking similarities to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer holding his hands up to the United fans just days before he was sacked following the 4-1 defeat at Watford five years ago . A proud and respected former player left hurting by the decline at Old Trafford? It’s happening again, and everyone appears to have accepted Carrick’s days are numbered. Perhaps the surest sign of that is not just Fernandes rounding on his manager but Carrick actually saying something interesting in his response when asked about his captain’s comments. “There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren’t going to win,” replied said, pointedly. But it has taken less than 150 days since the end of last season for disharmony to fester and the cracks in the dressing room to show. Carrick took over from the dismal reign of Ruben Amorim in January and inspired United's finishing third in the Premier League . The transformation of their form led to Fernandes finishing being named as the country’s player of the year. But United are now seven games without a win. Fernandes looks exhausted to be playing three times a week, as a result of their qualification for the Champions League. You could say Fernandes is genuinely hurt at how quickly things have unravelled, again. He has turned 32 this season and the majority of his United career has played out in this lingering sense of doom. But there was optimism heading into the summer after finishing third and Carrick laying the foundations; it is not his fault, or Carrick’s, that United appear to have messed up their midfield rebuild and failed to sign a left back or a back-up striker in the summer, which is the reason that Fernandes has been once again shifted out of his preferred No 10 position. Carrick apologised to the United fans for an ‘unacceptable’ performance in Italy (Getty) But it is significant that the Portuguese has rounded upon Carrick in the same manner of Lisandro Martinez ’s explosive criticism of Jason Wilcox a week ago . Martinez took the extraordinary step of criticising those upstairs and singling out United’s technical director for not backing Carrick in the transfer market. Martinez’s rant struck a chord with the United support, but he was still swiftly frog-marched into a Carrington office for a meeting with Wilcox, CEO Omar Berrada, and Carrick before apologising. Carrick hailed a “fresh start” after the 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday . He insisted, only last Friday, that his players had their best training session under him. But that facade of a harmonious camp has unravelled as quickly as this disjointed United side and morale is on the floor. Fernandes has reverted, quite stunningly, really, from last season's talisman to the demonstrative, moaning figurehead, whose this-is-all-quite-crap energy appears to be incredibly unhelpful in a time of crisis. And of course the roots of United’s permacrisis run much deeper than Carrick, as Martinez alluded to last week in Madrid. Like his Argentinian team-mate, Fernandes could have come out and criticised the United owners and their hierarchy and torched the decisions and processes that have led to the club’s worst start to a season since 1986. But Martinez tried that last week and it was like shouting into the wind. Instead, Fernandes chose to expose what appears to be division in a fractured dressing room, and even Carrick appeared resigned into accepting there’s no coming back from that.

item.title: Europa League: Juventus vs. Rennes – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV
item.description: Europa League: Juventus vs. Rennes – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade will start together for the first time in the Juventus attack as the Bianconeri host Rennes at the Allianz Stadium in the Europa League Round 3. It kicks off at 18:45 CET [17:45 BST] at the Allianz Stadium in Turin. The Bianconeri have already won the opening two Europa League games in the league phase, but want to bounce back after a 3-0 home loss against Lazio in Serie A last Sunday. TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Kolo Muani of Juventus in action against Nuno Tavares of SS Lazio during the Serie A match between Juventus and SS Lazio at Allianz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) The Old Lady’s coach Luciano Spalletti confirmed on Wednesday that Kolo Muani and Woltemade would start together for the first time today. Spalletti is still dealing with a selection crisis, with Francisco Conceiçao, Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Kamil Grabara and Jeff Ekhator injured. Edon Zhegrova, Daniele Rugani and Arkadiusz Milik are also unavailable because they are not on the Bianconeri’s UEFA list. TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Nick Woltemade of Juventus runs with the ball under pressure from Reda Belahyane of S.S. Lazio during the Serie A match between Juventus and SS Lazio at Allianz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images) According to multiple sources, including Tuttosport, Gazzetta and Sky , Gleison Bremer will start at the back, joined by Federico Gatti and Lloyd Kelly. There’s doubt on the right flank over whether Pierre Kalulu or Zeki Celik will start, while Andrea Cambiaso is expected to play as a left midfielder. Douglas Luiz and Pape Matar Sarr will compete for a starting spot in central midfield alongside Teun Koopmeiners. Juventus vs. Rennes – where to watch on TV The match is available on TNT Sports 5, HBO Max, and NOW TV in the UK and Ireland, and on CBS Sports Network, Paramount+, fuboTV, TUDN USA, TUDN.com, the TUDN App, and ViX in the USA. Football Italia will provide live updates via a live blog with Bournemouth-Milan and Ajax-Atalanta (Conference League) to follow at 21:00 CET. Juventus vs. Rennes – probable line-ups Juventus (3-4-1-2): Vicario; Gatti, Bremer, Kelly; Kalulu, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners, Celik; McKennie; Woltemade, Kolo Muani. Rennes (3-5-2): Samba; Ait Boudlal, Cresswell, Rouault; Reynolds; Szymanski, Rongier, M. Camara, Nagida; Dia, Al-Taamari.

item.title: Crystal Palace XI vs Besiktas – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Crystal Palace XI vs Besiktas – Predicted lineup and team news Crystal Palace will be aiming to recover from their slim Europa League losses when they travel to Turkey to take on Besiktas on Thursday at the Tupras Stadyumu. The Eagles arrive for this European fixture in a difficult spell after a run of disappointing displays. They were beaten heavily 5-0 by rivals Brighton in their most recent match, exposing major problems in a defence that is already short of players. With Pierre Sage’s team lacking rhythm and belief both at home and in Europe, they are under serious pressure to regain stability and improve defensively. Crystal Palace team news Palace head into the game with a major lack of defensive options for Sage. Chadi Riad is still sidelined with a knee injury, while Dean Henderson, Ben Chilwell, and Takehiro Tomiyasu were all absent against Brighton and remain unavailable. Axel Disasi is back after serving a domestic ban and should lead a temporary back three, joined by Jaydee Canvot and Chris Richards in front of goalkeeper Walter Benítez. Further forward, Sage can call on Mingueza, Mitchell, Timber, and Wharton across the midfield and wide areas. Yeremy Pino and Ismaïla Sarr are expected to provide width and support Jørgen Strand Larsen through the middle. Jean-Philippe Mateta and Daichi Kamada are also realistic alternatives as Sage decides on his strongest attacking setup. Crystal Palace predicted lineup Possible starting XI: Henderson; Canvot, Disasi, Richards; Mingueza, Timber, Wharton, Mitchell; Pino, Sarr; Strand Larsen When will the match kick off? The match will kick off at 8pm BST on Thursday, 23rd October. How to watch Besiktas vs Crystal Palace? The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 2 for UK fans. item.title: Wrong anthems played at Asian Para Games after mishap-marred Asian Games
item.description: The Asian Games closed on October 4 (MOHD RASFAN) Wrong national anthems were played three times at the Asian Para Games in Japan's Nagoya this week, prompting the mayor to apologise just days after the city hosted the mishap-plagued Asian Games. The Asian Para Games is taking place in the central Japanese hub city through Saturday, featuring around 4,000 athletes and officials in 18 sports. Nagoya Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa apologised on Wednesday for the latest error, which occurred despite officials' pledges to implement steps to prevent mistakes, including playing the correct national anthems. "These things happened during the Asian Games, so of course the operations were reviewed and examined based on the lessons learned. The fact that it happened again is really just unacceptable," the mayor told a press conference. On Monday, a Taiwanese athlete won a men's para taekwondo competition, but the Iranian anthem was played in its entirety, according to Nagoya officials at the mayor's press conference. Officials realised their mistake after the ceremony, they said. On the same day, the Iranian anthem was played again during a women's para taekwondo ceremony, where a Mongolian competitor was receiving the gold medal, according to the city. The incorrect music was stopped after the Mongolian delegation pointed out the error. Organisers then played the Mongolian anthem after the music was provided by the delegation, Nagoya officials said. Separately on Monday, officials broadcast the South Korean anthem for about five seconds, instead of the Chinese one, before a sitting volleyball match between China and Iran. "It is unacceptable, or rather, it's painful. I am very sorry about it," the mayor said, adding that he felt the tournament was otherwise progressing smoothly. The Asian Games, which concluded in early October, faced heavy criticism for shortcomings ranging from inadequate accommodation for athletes to the playing of wrong national anthems. On September 18, organisers played North Korea's national anthem for the South Korean hockey team. hih/hol

item.title: Besiktas vs Crystal Palace – Match preview and team news
item.description: Besiktas vs Crystal Palace – Match preview and team news Crystal Palace will look to bounce back from their narrow defeats in the Europa League last time out when they face Besiktas away from home on Thursday at the Tupras Stadyumu. Besiktas vs Crystal Palace – Match preview and team news Date: Thursday, 23rd October. Kick-off: 8pm BST. Venue: Tupras Stadyumu, Istanbul. Besiktas team news Besiktas faces notable selection challenges ahead of their Europa League clash under head coach Vincenzo Italiano. The Turkish side will definitely be missing club captain Orkun Kökçü, who remains sidelined with a foot and heel injury sustained during their previous European fixture against Hoffenheim. Adding to their woes, winger Milot Rashica is completely ruled out of the contest due to a persistent thigh and hamstring muscle injury. On a positive note, former Juventus striker Dušan Vlahović is back in contention after recovering from the illness that kept him out of the Hoffenheim victory. Vlahović is expected to battle Oh Hyeon-gyu to lead the frontline, while Leandro Trossard is heavily tipped to start on the left wing. Despite Kökçü being named in some projected lineups alongside Nübel, Murillo, Agbadou, and Topcu, his official absence means Italiano must engineer a late tactical adjustment in midfield. Crystal Palace team news Crystal Palace enters the fixture plagued by a severe defensive shortage for manager Pierre Sage. The Eagles remain without long-term absentee Chadi Riad due to a knee injury. Furthermore, key defensive figures Dean Henderson, Ben Chilwell, and Takehiro Tomiyasu all missed the recent Brighton match and remain entirely unavailable for selection. To steady the backline, Axel Disasi returns from a domestic suspension and is expected to anchor a makeshift back three alongside young Jaydee Canvot and Chris Richards, shielding goalkeeper Walter Benítez. Further up the pitch, Sage has options with Mingueza, Mitchell, Timber, and Wharton anchoring the wider positions. In the attacking third, Yeremy Pino and Ismaïla Sarr are highly likely to feature out wide to support central forward Jørgen Strand Larsen, though Jean-Philippe Mateta and Daichi Kamada also remain firmly in the structural conversation for the final starting eleven. Form Besiktas is experiencing a turbulent run of form across all competitions. The Turkish side is looking to bounce back immediately after suffering a disappointing 2-0 domestic defeat against Trabzonspor over the weekend. Prior to that setback, Vincenzo Italiano’s squad secured a morale-boosting victory against Hoffenheim in their previous European fixture. They will need to rediscover that continental sharpness to overcome their recent domestic inconsistency and steady their group-stage campaign. Crystal Palace Crystal Palace enters this European clash in a state of crisis following a string of poor performances. item.title: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez will not travel to Barcelona for El Clasico
item.description: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez will not travel to Barcelona for El Clasico Real Madrid president Florentino Perez will not travel to Barcelona for Sunday’s El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou, according to Mundo Deportivo , meaning the Spanish giants will contest one of football’s biggest fixtures without a meeting between the two clubs’ presidents. The traditional pre-match lunch involving the Barcelona and Real Madrid boards will also not take place, which continues to show the massive breakdown in relations between the rivals. Real Madrid will maintain a presence at Camp Nou Perez’s decision not to attend means there will be no presidential reunion with Barcelona counterpart Joan Laporta before kick-off. However, it is crucial to note that a Real Madrid delegate is expected to represent the club in the VIP area, ensuring that the club will still have an official presence at the stadium. Florentino Perez will not attend the El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) There is precedent for a reduced Madrid delegation. At the previous corresponding Clasico at Camp Nou, Real Madrid honorary president Pirri was the club’s sole representative in the VIP box. The expected attendance of a new delegate this time would again leave Perez away from the occasion. For Real Madrid, the priority is the match itself, as the president’s absence does not alter the sporting challenge facing the team, although it will attract attention given the significance of the rivalry and the current state of relations between the two institutions. Negreira dispute continues to affect relations with Barcelona The lack of a directors’ lunch shows the declining institutional relationship between the two that has developed since Real Madrid became involved in the Negreira case . There is no relationship between Real Madrid and Barcelona. (Photo by LLUIS GENE/AFP via Getty Images) The dispute has contributed to the deterioration in relations between the clubs , with the traditional pre-match gathering between their leadership teams no longer taking place. Perez has also been absent from Camp Nou in recent seasons, making his latest decision consistent with that pattern. The lack of direct engagement between the presidents means there is little indication of an immediate return to the previous level of cooperation between the clubs. Indeed, the situation remains separate from the footballing contest, but it illustrates how the rivalry has extended beyond the pitch into the boardroom.

item.title: Champions League Team of the Week: Our Best XI
item.description: Champions League Team of the Week: Our Best XI The Champions League delivered another week of drama, statement victories and individual brilliance, with established superstars and emerging talents alike making their mark on Europe's biggest stage. From Phil Foden 's clinical hat-trick to Nico Paz 's sensational display for Como, there were performances that demanded recognition. Here is our Champions League Team of the Week, featuring the standout performers from another memorable round of European action. Goalkeeper: Yann Sommer - Club Brugge Club Brugge's 3-0 win over Lens looked like a comfortable result on paper, in large part thanks to Yann Sommer. The veteran made a string of saves to deny the French side, who created six big chances without scoring. Right-back: Federico Valverde - Real Madrid Influential at both ends as Real Madrid made light work of Leipzig at the Bernabeu. Valverde led the contest for touches (116), made three key passes, five clearances, and four tackles on a characteristically all-action night. Centre-back: Jacobo Ramon - Como Expect the queue of clubs interested in Jacobo Ramon to get a little longer. A standout showing against Manchester United saw the Spanish centre-back lead the game for touches (103) and make a whopping 12 line-breaking passes. Late on, he ghosted forward to head home the fourth goal of an unforgettable win. Centre-back: Natan - Real Betis Real Betis maintained their 100% record in the Champions League this season with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Feyenoord. The Spanish side are back in this competition for the first time since 2005/06 and are making an impression. Natan led the side to a clean sheet, with 18 defensive actions, nine clearances, and just one misplaced pass. Left-back: Carlos Augusto - Inter Milan A brilliant breakaway goal from Carlos Augusto earned Inter a 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk, as the Italian champions recovered from Alessandro Bastoni's red card to win. Augusto became just the third Inter defender to score in consecutive Champions League appearances, after Giacinto Facchetti in 1967 and Denzel Dumfries in 2025. Midfield: Vitinha - Paris Saint-Germain The conductor of the best side in Europe. PSG will take some stopping in the chase for Champions League success, as the champions target a third straight crown. Vitinha was at his elusive best against Barcelona and capped a fine performance with a stunning goal. Midfield: Phil Foden - Manchester City How good is it to see Phil Foden back enjoying his football? One of the most watchable talents in the Premier League has had a tough time of late, but this was Foden back at his best. A clinical hat-trick helped Manchester City cruised past AEK Athens and bodes well for Enzo Maresca's in-form side. An outstanding showing from Paz, who became the youngest Argentinian player (22 years, 43 days) to be involved in three goals (2 goals, 1 assist) in a Champions League game since Messi in 2009. Desire Doue was the star of the show for PSG, opening the scoring with a strike from outside the box before later assisting Lucas Hernandez from a corner. Forward: Harry Kane - Bayern Munich Has a good a chance as anyone of taking the Ballon d'Or next week. Kane cut apart Arsenal with an exquisite pass for Alphonso Davies' equaliser, before scoring the second from the spot to continue his fine record against the Gunners.

item.title: Liverpool's next transfer is obvious, Fabrizio Romano confirms it
item.description: Liverpool's next transfer is obvious, Fabrizio Romano confirms it Liverpool spent over £150 million on new players in the summer. In a normal season, this would allow Liverpool to add many new faces to their ranks but, this time around, only four were brought. In fact, the deal for Jeremy Jacquet was completed in January 2026 so, his transfer fee can't even be counted towards the total amount they spent. And, while Jacquet, Ronald Araujo, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola have all had a positive impact on Liverpool since joining, there are still some positions among their ranks that could do with an upgrade or two. This has been made clear for a while now but, since the Reds don't have an endless money pit like some of their rivals, it's unclear whether the transfers they need to make will actually be completed in January. But, fortunately for the Reds' fanbase, some transfers do seem to be on the horizon. Fabrizio Romano admits that Liverpool's search for a new midfielder is becoming 'intense' Fabrizio Romano is the transfer guru. The Italian journalist was the first to break the news of Araujo joining Liverpool and, aside from his 'here we go' on Marc Guehi last season, his news about Liverpool has often been fairly accurate. Whether its about a change of manager or a player exiting/joining, Romano has often been on point. So, the fact that he's now said conversations about Liverpool signing a new midfielder have become 'intense' could mean that a January deal for one is on the way. "Conversations on midfielders are becoming very very intense at Liverpool. We’ll have to wait and see whether it will be for January or the summer," he said via his YouTube channel . "Lamine Camara and Alex Scott are appreciated." Liverpool must do everything they can to sign a new midfielder soon At the moment, Liverpool have four central midfielders among their ranks. Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister are Iraola's two preferred options at the moment but, with Szoboszlai now out of action for who knows how long, others such as Ryan Gravenberch and even Trey Nyoni may be given a more regular role. And, as well as Nyoni has played this season, relying on him to be a regular starter at just 19 years old feels a tad unfair. So, signing a new central midfielder such as Alex Scott, Adam Wharton or Lamine Camara should be one of their top priorities . Because, not only would it help improve their standing but, it could also help them get back to their best, especially since squad depth was one of their main issues last term. For now, everything is still up in the air but, with Romano saying that things have become "intense" at Liverpool regarding their search for a midfielder, it certainly feels like a new number six is on the top of Julian Ward's agenda.

item.title: Nagelsmann emerges as leading candidate to replace Carrick amid Man United crisis
item.description: Nagelsmann emerges as leading candidate to replace Carrick amid Man United crisis Michael Carrick is under huge pressure as Manchester United coach after a 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday extended the Red Devils’ winless run to seven games. According to talkSPORT, Manchester United are seemingly already preparing for life without Carrick and have identified former Bayern Munich and Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann as their leading candidate to replace him. The 39-year-old, who left his role as Germany boss following a disappointing World Cup, was linked with the job before Carrick was appointed permanently in May and is understood to have admirers within the club’s hierarchy. Another German coach, Brighton & Hove Albion boss Fabian Hürzeler, is also being mentioned as a candidate, alongside Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe.

item.title: Warriors’ Draymond Green weighs in on Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic flare-up
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Warriors’ Draymond Green weighs in on Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic flare-up appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg did not hold back his frustration toward Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic during his debut game. The two players were seen exchanging words on the court . However, Warriors veteran Draymond Green stood firmly behind his rookie teammate and defended his decision to challenge the Slovenian star. When asked about the heated exchange between Lendeborg and Doncic in the locker room, Green expressed his support for the rookie and dismissed the idea that he should have avoided confronting an established NBA superstar. “Everybody’s gonna be like, ‘Oh man, he shouldn’t talk to Luka,” Green said. “You should not talk to Luka. And I disagree with that shit, 1,000%. You fuc*** go and talk to somebody. You talk until you can’t fuc**** talk no more. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “And if he busts your a**, guess what? You play him again three more times, and you go back at his a** again. And then you see him the third time, and you go back at his a** again.” Lendeborg’s frustration with Doncic extended beyond their on-court confrontation. During his postgame press conference, the Warriors rookie made an even stronger statement about the Lakers superstar, claiming that he had lost all respect for the Slovenian guard after playing against him in his first regular-season NBA game. Meanwhile, Warriors superstar Stephen Curry also expressed his support for Lendeborg. “So he’s setting the table for himself to have to show up, and I like that nature of the game, whether you do it in between your ears or you let it out, I know he’ll be able to back it up,” Curry said. Unfortunately for Lendeborg, his NBA debut ended in a loss as the Warriors fell 125-107 to the Lakers. Despite the disappointing team result, the rookie delivered a respectable individual performance, finishing with 12 points on 5-of-11 shooting from the field, along with three rebounds. The 0-1 Warriors will now look to bounce back from their season-opening loss when they take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday. Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

item.title: 'Let's not kid ourselves!' - Bernardo Silva sounds El Clasico alarm as midfielder nets first Real Madrid goal in Champions League rout
item.description: Real Madrid v Sevilla FC - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bernardo Silva opened his Real Madrid account during a commanding 4-1 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig. However, the Portuguese midfielder is already turning his attention to a crucial El Clasico showdown against Barcelona. The playmaker stressed that Jose Mourinho's men must refine their tactical balance ahead of a fixture that could dictate the La Liga title race. Silva opens account in commanding Leipzig win Real Madrid secured a 4-1 Champions League triumph over RB Leipzig on matchday three, but the scoreline flattered the hosts following a shaky start. The Bundesliga outfit repeatedly threatened during the opening 45 minutes, forcing Thibaut Courtois into vital interventions to keep his side level. Following the interval, Los Blancos finally clicked into gear. Silva found the net right before the break to register his first goal for the Spanish giants since his summer move from Man City, helping seal a comprehensive European victory. Despite the emphatic result, the playmaker acknowledged that the squad is still searching for tactical harmony as they integrate their array of attacking talent. Striking the perfect tactical balance Speaking to Movistar Plus+ after the final whistle, Bernardo highlighted the struggle of managing a squad packed with individual flair. "It’s difficult to strike a balance between controlling the game and not being a boring team," he explained. "We’re a team with players who are very aggressive individually in one-on-one situations, who like to dribble and find space. We need to strike a balance between keeping possession and pushing forward, being direct. "That balance between controlling the game and not being a boring team, whilst remaining intense and aggressive, is difficult and we have to be very well prepared." Reflecting on his milestone goal and the team's sluggish start, the former Man City midfielder praised his goalkeeper. "I’m very happy to have won this match and scored my first goal in this shirt. It was a difficult match; we were much better in the second half than in the first," Bernardo noted. "In the first half, we let them get into our box quite a few times and Thibaut was crucial." FBL-EUR-C1-REAL MADRID-LEIPZIG Trophies demand a united squad With Real Madrid aiming to compete on all fronts, Bernardo stressed the importance of building collective belief. "It’s good to feel that the team remains confident and is improving. I think we’re improving quite a lot; it’s only the start of the season," he said. "We need to keep winning game by game so that, in the last three or four months, we can be in the running for trophies - which is what this club demands of you." item.title: Rams’ Davante Adams holding off on hamstring surgery until ‘best time,’ per Sean McVay
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Rams’ Davante Adams holding off on hamstring surgery until ‘best time,’ per Sean McVay appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams ’ season is quickly spiralling out of control. Pegged as the top contender to win the Super Bowl this year, Los Angeles’ season is in danger of dying before the halfway point of the season. They are 2-4 after six games and currently sit at the bottom of their division. It’s safe to say that this isn’t where the Rams expected to be at this point of the season. To make matters worse, one of their star players will be out for a meaningful time due to an injury. Star wide receiver Davante Adams suffered a ruptured hamstring in Week 6 and is now out for an extended period of time. Adams has already undergone surgery to repair his hamstring. According to Rams head coach Sean McVay, though, Adams will need an extra procedure. “Sean McVay said Davante Adams will need a “cleanup” procedure on his hamstring but it has not been scheduled yet.” Sarah Barshop reported on X. “‘I think they’re going to give it a couple days and figure out exactly when is the best time,’ McVay said.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Adams’ injury is just the latest addition to the long list of injuries and troubles that the Rams have been dealing with this season. They have already played the majority of the 2026 season without Myles Garrett, who underwent knee surgery earlier this year. They’ve also dealt with other injuries this season, but Garrett’s and Adams’ injuries are the most consequential of them all. Even when they were completely healthy, though, the Rams have been struggling. Adams suffered the injury in their Week 6 game against the Cardinals, but the Los Angeles offense was already struggling before that injury happened. A combination of special teams mishaps and stagnation on offense has led to this supposed superteam struggling to generate any momentum this year. The Rams have a chance to bounce back in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders. On paper, the Rams should be a better team. However, this better team on paper has struggled to put away teams as of late. Can the shorthanded team bounce back? item.content:encoded: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Rams’ Davante Adams holding off on hamstring surgery until ‘best time,’ per Sean McVay appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams ’ season is quickly spiralling out of control. Pegged as the top contender to win the Super Bowl this year, Los Angeles’ season is in danger of dying before the halfway point of the season. They are 2-4 after six games and currently sit at the bottom of their division. It’s safe to say that this isn’t where the Rams expected to be at this point of the season. To make matters worse, one of their star players will be out for a meaningful time due to an injury. Star wide receiver Davante Adams suffered a ruptured hamstring in Week 6 and is now out for an extended period of time. Adams has already undergone surgery to repair his hamstring. According to Rams head coach Sean McVay, though, Adams will need an extra procedure. “Sean McVay said Davante Adams will need a “cleanup” procedure on his hamstring but it has not been scheduled yet.” Sarah Barshop reported on X. “‘I think they’re going to give it a couple days and figure out exactly when is the best time,’ McVay said.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Adams’ injury is just the latest addition to the long list of injuries and troubles that the Rams have been dealing with this season. They have already played the majority of the 2026 season without Myles Garrett, who underwent knee surgery earlier this year. They’ve also dealt with other injuries this season, but Garrett’s and Adams’ injuries are the most consequential of them all. Even when they were completely healthy, though, the Rams have been struggling. Adams suffered the injury in their Week 6 game against the Cardinals, but the Los Angeles offense was already struggling before that injury happened. A combination of special teams mishaps and stagnation on offense has led to this supposed superteam struggling to generate any momentum this year. The Rams have a chance to bounce back in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders. On paper, the Rams should be a better team. However, this better team on paper has struggled to put away teams as of late. Can the shorthanded team bounce back? item.title: Arteta gives depressing Saka injury update
item.description: Arteta gives depressing Saka injury update Bukayo Saka lasted only 10 minutes of Arsenal’s Champions League draw at Bayern Munich, with Mikel Arteta offering a worrying assessment afterwards. Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images Arsenal fans are facing an anxious wait after Bukayo Saka suffered a quadriceps injury during Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw away to Bayern Munich , with Mikel Arteta admitting afterwards that the problem “doesn’t look good at all”. Saka lasted only 10 minutes at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night before being forced off with an injury to his left thigh. There was no challenge involved. The winger went down immediately after playing a pass and grabbed his thigh just above the knee before receiving treatment on the pitch. He was unable to continue and headed down the tunnel after Eberechi Eze replaced him, with the match still goalless at that point. Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images Arteta confirmed after the game that the injury was to Saka’s quadriceps rather than his hamstring. “It’s his quad,” Arteta said . “It was early in the game, and the level of intensity his game requires is something incredible. The quality, strength and attention you need has to be at the highest level, and those things happen unfortunately. It doesn’t look good at all, but we have to wait and see.” The Arsenal manager offered little reassurance when speaking separately to TNT Sports . “They are a bit concerned,” he said. “A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.” Arsenal are now waiting for a further assessment before they can establish how long Saka might be unavailable. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images

item.title: Bayern coach Kompany doesn't expect long Díaz and Kim absence
item.description: Bayern Munich's Luis Diaz leaves the field during the Champions League soccer match between FC Bayern Munich and Arsenal at the Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern coach Kompany doesn't expect long Díaz and Kim absence») Sven Hoppe/dpa Bayern Munich winger Luis Díaz and defender Kim Minjae are not expected to be sidelined for a long time as coach Vincent Kompany suggested they could be back for next week's big Bundesliga match against Borussia Dortmund. "I hope it is similar time-wise for both. That means not so long, maybe less than a week," Kompany said after Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal. Medical examinations were to follow but Kompany said "I believe that very severe injuries can be ruled out." Kim started against Arsenal despite not being fully fit and lasted only the first half. Díaz, who did not start owing to muscular problems, came on in the 68th but was substituted again late in the game. The match against Dortmund is on October 31. Before that comes Sunday's match at third-placed Freiburg which Díaz and Kim are set to miss. Champions Bayern top the table on goal difference ahead of Dortmund, with Freiburg and Bayer Leverkusen one point behind.

item.title: Santos grab sixth straight victory after defeating Pumas in controversial fashion
item.description: TORREON, MEXICO - OCTOBER 21: Eduardo Aguirre of Santos celebrates after scoring the first goal of his team during the Liga MX Torneo Apertura 2026 13th-round match between Santos Laguna and Pumas at Corona Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Torreon, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Guadarrama/Getty Images) | Getty Images Santos Laguna won their sixth straight match for the first time in short tournaments after defeating Pumas by a 2-0 score. In a match filled with controversy from the first minute of play, Santos got a victory that now has them a single point from getting into the Liguilla zone. Santos will have a tough match to try to continue their streak when they travel west to face Tijuana while Pumas will host Tigres in a match where both teams look likely to miss out on the post season. The first half started with Pumas having the return of Cesar Huerta to the starting 11 after being suspended in their last match against Atlante. Less than a minute into the match, Pumas got caught in a counter and Ezequiel Bullaude got into the area where Nathan seemed to have tripped him and the referee gave a Penalty Kick to Santos and gave red card to Nathan, leaving Pumas with 10 players. Replays showed the push had been minimal and it was no way a red card offense, even with the supposed being a clear goal opportunity but the controversial call stood. Eduardo Aguirre stepped up to take the PK and got off a right footed shot past Pumas’ goalkeeper, Keylor Navas to score and give Santos the 1-0 lead. Off a corner kick, the cross into the area was volleyed wide by Diego Gonzalez. Because of injury, Santos subbed out Efrain Orona for Jonathan Perez. Huerta would get into the area and get off a left footed shot that forced a good save from Santos’ goalkeeper, Carlos Acevedo. Santos kept dominating possession but created few chances while Pumas sat back and defended. The halftime whistle blew as Santos looked incredibly cautious for a match at home with a man advantage. The 2nd half started with Santos subbing out Diego Gonzalez for Emmanuel Echeverria. A couple of minutes into the half, Pumas had to sub out an injured Adalberto Carrasquilla for Victor Arteaga. A rabona cross from Huerta turned into a shot that was saved by Acevedo. A free kick into the area was headed by Uriel Antuna directly to Acevedo. Santos subbed out Tahiel Jimenez and Fran Villalba for Esteban Lozano and Aldo Lopez. A run into the area ended with a cross by Mauricio Cuevas that turned into a shot that Navas saved. Pumas subbed out Rodrigo Lopez for Alvaro Angulo. item.title: Stephen A. Smith says he already knows when LeBron James is going to retire
item.description: Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images LeBron James just started his 24th season in the NBA. The basketball icon, who is the GOAT in some people’s eyes, extended his own record when he played for the Philadelphia 76ers in their season opener against the New York Knicks. James is taking things season by season at the moment and has made no announcement about when he plans on retiring. But Stephen A. Smith thinks he knows when that will be. Stephen A. Smith says LeBron James will retire after his 25th season Smith and James have had their conflicts over the years, but what nobody can deny is their deep love for basketball. The TV personality always has something to say about the games he watches, and it was no different after the Sixers beat the Knicks on the opening night. James’ debut was always going to be a hot topic of discussion, and Smith admitted on ESPN that he really liked seeing The King play as a center. Using that, the presenter has come up with a theory on when James is going to retire. He said: “I love the role that LeBron played and his willingness to be that big guy that’s defending other bigs. “He has gotten big, as you can see, because he recognises the fact that he’s going to be spending most of his time at the four-to-five position playing for this particular team. So, I get that part. “And because he’s in his 24th season, age 42 (actually 41), these are the last two years of his career. He’s going to play a quarter century. That’s the goal. Play 25 years and then walk away, retire. “You know that he’s not trying to be out there every night running up and down the court. That’s not what he’s going to do.” Retiring after 25 years at the top would be an exceptional achievement, but James has not closed the door on playing for another year. “When I’m done, will it be 24 years? 25 years? 26 years? Who knows? We’ll see when I’m finished,” James said earlier in 2026. item.title: Today's 5️⃣: Madrid run riot, Betis win and Boca learn their opponents
item.description: Today's 5️⃣: Madrid run riot, Betis win and Boca learn their opponents Good morning, football fans. The third round of Champions League matches wrapped up yesterday, and there’s plenty to talk about at home and abroad. Here are the day’s top 5 stories. Let’s get started. Real Madrid cruise to emphatic win over Leipzig Los Blancos enjoyed a brilliant night in Europe with a convincing victory over RB Leipzig. They controlled the game from the opening whistle and were ruthlessly effective in attack. The tactical game plan worked to perfection on the pitch. Their high press repeatedly forced the German side to give the ball away, allowing the home attackers to pose a constant threat. 📸 Diego Souto - 2026 Getty Images The win gives Real Madrid a confidence boost heading into El Clásico next Sunday, October 25. Betis beat Feyenoord and keep making history Betis still have a perfect record in the Champions League. Manuel Pellegrini ’s men edged past Feyenoord thanks to an Isco penalty and continue to dream big. 📸 JORGE GUERRERO - AFP or licensors The road ahead is tough, but not impossible: Dortmund, Slovan Bratislava, Como, Arsenal and Bayern. The build-up to El Clásico heats up This Sunday’s El Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou will have plenty of talking points, including José Mourinho’s return to Barcelona. The clash between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid will also be marked by tensions between the clubs’ leadership: Florentino Pérez will not travel to Barcelona, so there will be no reunion with Joan Laporta. 📸 Angel Martinez - 2025 Getty Images Real Sociedad and Celta de Vigo prepare for European action A demanding day awaits Spain’s representatives in Europe. Real Sociedad and Celta de Vigo are putting the finishing touches to their preparations for this afternoon’s UEFA Europa League fixtures. Both teams are chasing their first win in the competition: Matarazzo’s side have one point, while Claudio Giráldez’s men have none. Atlético Mineiro reach Sudamericana final; Palmeiras reach Libertadores final The finalists in South America’s two continental competitions are taking shape. Atlético Mineiro booked their place in the Copa Sudamericana final after edging past Montevideo City Torque 3-2 on aggregate. The final is now confirmed: Boca Juniors vs Atlético Mineiro in Barranquilla. 📸 Ernesto Ryan - 2026 Getty Images Meanwhile, the Copa Libertadores clash between Palmeiras and Fluminense went down to the wire, with the Verdão securing their place in the final in a penalty shootout. Palmeiras await the winner of today’s meeting between Flamengo and Estudiantes. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Tresoldi has time to decide international future, insists Klopp
item.description: Tresoldi has time to decide international future, insists Klopp Jürgen Klopp has described Nicolo Tresoldi as a “world-class talent” following the striker’s hat-trick against Inter Milan a week ago, but has urged caution over the debate surrounding his international future. Tresoldi’s impressive performance has intensified interest in which national team he will ultimately represent. However, Klopp believes that the attention should not become a burden for the young forward as he considers such an important decision. “Tresoldi is a world-class talent, but there is no point putting pressure on the lad because of his decision about which national team he wants to play for,” Klopp said. The Germany coach stressed that Tresoldi is currently involved with the under-21 team and has time to decide what is best for his future. “He is with the under-21s for now and has time. But yes, he has outstanding qualities, and we want to give him the peace and space he needs to make this important decision.” With his performances attracting growing attention, Tresoldi’s international future is likely to remain a talking point. For now, however, Klopp wants the youngster to concentrate on his development and make his choice in his own time.

item.title: The Young Bucks BULLDOZED In Brutally Short AEW Dynamite SQUASH! (AEW News)
item.description: AEW While the Young Bucks may have retained the AEW Tag Team Titles against the Don Callis Family's Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher at WrestleDream this past weekend, the Bucks were completely decimated by two other Callis Family men on last night's Dynamite. There, Matt and Nick Jackson faced off against Mark Davis and Jake Doyle in a title eliminator match that didn't even last three minutes. From the get-go, Davis and Doyle took control of this one and put a beating on the Young Bucks around the ringside area, with Matt Jackson thrown into a barricade, and Nick Jackson powerbombed through the timekeeper's table. And once the action finally hit the ring, Davis hit Matt with three of his patented piledrivers, as Doyle grabbed a bearhug on Nick. That was the end of the match, as Davis pinned Matt Jackson, and Doyle put one foot on Nick Jackson to get the simultaneous three-count on the Bucks. The story here was that the Young Bucks were coming into this match banged up from their WrestleDream defence against Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher, and they'd only just been cleared to compete. Either way, this victory for Mark Davis and Jake Doyle was one of the most dominant in AEW history, and put the two on course for a shot at the AEW Tag Team Titles at Full Gear on Saturday, November 14th. Likewise, all four of Davis, Doyle, and the Bucks are expected to be involved at Blood & Guts on November 4th. All Future PLC brands are supported by its audience. item.title: Leam Richardson Praises Reading’s Defence In 1-0 Leyton Orient Win
item.description: The Royals secured a brilliant 1-0 victory over Leyton Orient at the SCL Stadium to move into the League One play-off places. A second-half strike from Paddy Lane proved to be the difference, although the Royals could have enjoyed a more comfortable victory after Lewis Wing saw his first-half penalty saved. The victory moves Reading up to sixth in the table. Royals boss Leam Richardson spoke to Royals TV to share his thoughts on the performance and another important three points. Richardson on the victory “Yeah, a good response from the weekend. The result, not the performance, but yeah, clean sheets – I love clean sheets! “I thought we worked hard, certainly in the second half. We started the game really well. I thought we were really good with the ball and without the ball, and caused them all sorts of problems. “I think they changed shape a couple of times as well, which is always a good sign of respect. We’re probably disappointed not to go in at half-time one or two goals up. “In the second half, we had to be really good without the ball. Although it looked like they had some good shots, I don’t really remember Joel having to make any massive saves. “I thought we were quite comfortable controlling the ball. We probably started to play the result a little bit for 20 minutes, but that’s human nature. We’re at home and we’re trying everything we can to win. “We made changes to get us back up the pitch a little bit, and the lads who came on did their jobs really well. “The goal was a typical team goal. Our possession, controlling the spaces where we wanted to be, and then in transition, it was fantastic. A really good team goal, so I’m really pleased.” Richardson on Lewis Wing’s missed penalty “Listen, we’ve got good players. We knew there was nothing lost, nothing gained. We’ve got to stay strong with it. “He’s very experienced, Wingy, isn’t he? So I’ve got no issues with that. He’ll take the next one. “He’s disappointed like everybody else, but I thought him and Andy in the middle of the pitch were excellent tonight, with and without the ball. “In the first half, they were fantastic. They made great decisions, changing play, and then I thought without the ball in the second half, the lads were really controlled. “The wide players on the outside, the nine and the 10 in front of them, I thought we were very good.” Richardson on the defensive performance and clean sheet “It’s not just about the back four and the goalkeeper, you need all 11. “You see how hard the lads work for 60 or 70 minutes, controlling where we wanted to put the ball for large parts of the game. I think it’s credit to everybody, all the way through to Joel. “We were very methodical in what we were doing without the ball in the last 20 minutes, so that was really pleasing. “I think we probably deserved the win off the back of our endeavour without the ball in the second half and the way we played in the first half.” Richardson the fans “I’ve got to say, towards the end, I felt

item.title: “It will be so sad” - MotoGP riders lament loss of Phillip Island
item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP riders have voiced their disappointment at Phillip Island’s impending departure from the championship, with many describing it as one of their favourite venues on the calendar. This weekend’s Australian Grand Prix marks MotoGP’s final visit to Phillip Island, with the series set to move to a revamped Adelaide street circuit next year. The 4.4km circuit has proved extremely popular with the grid, who have been won over by its high-speed layout, frequent elevation changes and old-school characteristics. The atmosphere at the venue located south of Melbourne adds to the appeal of the race, with its coastal setting and scenic views making it a distinctive stop on the MotoGP calendar. As the only Australian on the grid, Pramac’s Jack Miller showered praise on the Phillip Island Circuit and explained what makes the track so special for him. “[The emotions are] pretty high,” he said. “It’s probably one of the most iconic tracks on the calendar and produced arguably some of the best races we've ever seen in MotoGP. “Phillip Island is a track where if you haven't got the bike working amazing, you can still make up a bit of difference once you get the thing round up. Our bike turns pretty good. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo MotoGP riders have voiced their disappointment at Phillip Island’s impending departure from the championship, with many describing it as one of their favourite venues on the calendar. This weekend’s Australian Grand Prix marks MotoGP’s final visit to Phillip Island, with the series set to move to a revamped Adelaide street circuit next year. The 4.4km circuit has proved extremely popular with the grid, who have been won over by its high-speed layout, frequent elevation changes and old-school characteristics. The atmosphere at the venue located south of Melbourne adds to the appeal of the race, with its coastal setting and scenic views making it a distinctive stop on the MotoGP calendar. As the only Australian on the grid, Pramac’s Jack Miller showered praise on the Phillip Island Circuit and explained what makes the track so special for him. “[The emotions are] pretty high,” he said. “It’s probably one of the most iconic tracks on the calendar and produced arguably some of the best races we've ever seen in MotoGP. “Phillip Island is a track where if you haven't got the bike working amazing, you can still make up a bit of difference once you get the thing round up. Our bike turns pretty good. So as long as we can kind of get it round up and get it turning all right, you should be in with a shout. “This place is phenomenal, and on a MotoGP bike riding around here, it's something particular. You're kind of dancing with the bike the whole way through, trying to manage the shaking, the wheelie and the way the bike deals with the wind. “You can never fully attack. You're kind of just playing with the bike the whole time, which makes it all the more fun to ride. “I thought as ironic as it gets, we'd have fantastic weather throughout the weekend after what we've had the last couple of years with some trying conditions. But it doesn't look that way. Phillip Island is giving itself a proper send-off with some ever-changing conditions.” KTM’s Pedro Acosta said he puts Phillip Island in the same breath as legendary motorcycle tracks like Mugello, as he prepares to bid farewell to the venue. Asked how riders would feel on their last visit to Melbourne, Acosta said: “On one side, it will be beautiful for everyone; and on the other one, it will be so sad. “One of the best atmospheres around the whole calendar, the fans are so close to us. Also, the track is one of these legendary tracks around the championship, like Mugello, Jerez and other ones around. “It will be so sad that next year we don't come here.” Phillip Island track details Phillip Island track details Marc Marquez , a two-time winner of the Australian Grand Prix, described Phillip Island is a track that commands respect from riders. “It’s one of my favourites and I really enjoy it,” he said. “But it’s a very fast, very narrow track, where if you crash, you’re in the gravel in no time. “It’s one of those tracks that riders have a healthy respect for; it’s a bit like Holland too – you’ve got that respect for it. “The final section is the one that really impresses, especially on the first few laps, and it’ll continue to impress this year.” Marquez’s title rival Jorge Martin also highlighted the appeal of the wider Phillip Island experience, where riders often stay in rented holiday homes rather than conventional hotels. “I'm sure I will miss Phillip Island for the next few years. Maybe we will come back in the future, but for the moment I will miss it,” he said. “First of all, the track itself. It's nice to ride here. It's really different from what we are used to. It's really fast. You need to put a lot of technique to be fast here. Since I arrived here in Moto3, I always loved it. “Then, the place. The vibe here is great. Also, you're in a house with all this wildlife where you can surf and everything. So it's a nice place and I always enjoyed it.” While Phillip Island has a cult following within motorcycle racing, ageing facilities and limited accommodation options had cast doubt over its future for several years. This year, the state government of South Australia secured a new deal to move MotoGP away from Victoria, with the Adelaide street circuit that once staged Formula 1 races gearing up to host the premier class next year. While MotoGP riders have softened their stance on Adelaide after MotoGP allayed their safety concerns with an AI-generated onboard video, they admit they will miss the outgoing Phillip Island. Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing “Phillip Island was always a beautiful race for the show, for the TV and for the fans,” said Honda rider Luca Marini . “In some years, it was maybe the most beautiful race of the year. 2018, 2017, I don't remember well, but the races were unbelievable, and also later on. “It's always the [winners’] trophy; it's unbelievable. It's something that I always dream about, but unfortunately, I was not on the podium here, so let's try in the wet this year. “It will be another amazing trophy because I think it's still one piece with history, with a unique style that you can find. You can win only here, and for the riders, the trophy is always important.” Aprilia star Marco Bezzecchi added: “Normally, at beautiful tracks, you always have very beautiful races. Here the battles have always been amazing. “Last year, the race was fantastic. It was my first MotoGP podium [in Phillip Island] as well. So, it was good.” Phillip Island first hosted the Australian GP in 1989 and became a permanent fixture on the calendar in 1997, replacing Eastern Creek. This year will mark the 30th and final world championship race on the island. Read Also: MotoGP to stage demo at F1 United States Grand Prix MotoGP teams told Qatar Grand Prix expected to go ahead To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Courtois sends warning to Barcelona as Real Madrid prepare for El Clasico
item.description: Courtois sends warning to Barcelona as Real Madrid prepare for El Clasico Real Madrid kept up their perfect record in this UEFA Champions League campaign as they beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in their third League Phase game. Several players stood out for the Merengue side in this game, but despite the margin with which they won, it was not really an easy game. One of these players who impressed in this game was the goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, as he had to make several interventions, especially in the first half, to keep the visitors from scoring. However, he was still unable to keep a clean sheet as the Germans scored one goal in the second half. As MARCA has reported, the Belgian veteran also talked to the media after the game. He was quite confident for the upcoming game against Barcelona, especially after the team’s recent good run of form: “I think we’ve played some good matches, picked up some good wins and made a great comeback in Rome. We’re confident about what lies ahead, and we know it’s going to be a tough match. But if we want to close the gap in the league, we’ll have to go there and win.” “You never know until you actually play the match. I think we’re in a good place and full of confidence. They’ve been doing very well in the league, but I believe in our team and think we can go there and win. It’s true that we’re playing away from home, and that makes a difference, but I believe in our team. For me, Clásicos are always 50-50, even when one team comes into the match in better form than the other.” The Real Madrid captain put his support behind Vinicius Junior after another underwhelming performance from the Brazilian: “No, I think he’s looking to get back to his best, and I’m sure he’ll get there with the support of the team and the fans. I think he played well. I saw him making dangerous runs and creating threats, but things don’t always go your way. “There are only two players I know of who have been at their best almost every season: Cristiano and Messi. I’ve watched them perform at that level year after year, and even two of the greatest players in history have been criticised at various points. That’s football. I think Vinícius has been playing almost every game for nine years, so we have to help him get back to his best. But he’s the first to be happy, enjoy himself and work towards reaching his best level.” While admitting that Real Madrid have struggled away from home, the goalie also pointed to the team’s improving form ahead of a stretch of away games: “Home and away matches are always different, and we’ve found it more difficult to get results away from home, in places like Spain, Rome and Elche, followed by the two defeats against Betis. I think we deserved more against Betis. We lost, but we played well. “It’s true that we need to improve away from home, but I think we’re doing well now that we’re back after the international break. We’ll be eager for Sunday and for what lies ahead, because we have four away matches coming up,

Hopefully, he will be able to keep a clean sheet in that game, and help the Merengues get a win over their bitter rivals.

item.title: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a productive offseason, Yaxel Lendeborg made his debut for the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday. His first task? Try to stop Luka Doncic. It was an unenviable assignment for the rookie forward. But it was also a good test. Unfortunately for Lendeborg, he did not study enough, and Doncic made him pay for it . The Los Angeles Lakers blew out the Warriors, 127-105, at Crypto.com Arena. Lendeborg had 12 points, three rebounds, and two assists in 29 minutes. He was whistled for a technical foul for talking trash to Luka Doncic in the second quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the postgame interview, coach Steve Kerr pointed out the 24-year-old Lendeborg’s learning curve . “This was a great welcome-to-the-NBA game for him. Having to guard Luka, who is as tough to guard as anybody in the world. Having to learn all the little tricks that exist in the NBA. He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff,” said Kerr in the video posted by The Athletic’s Anthony Slater. “It’s his first game. He’s an unbelievable young guy, great talent. It was a frustrating night for him, but a lesson well learned, and he’ll get better from here.” Steve Kerr on Yaxel Lendeborg guarding Luka Doncic in his debut: “He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff.” Kerr didn’t like the technical on Yaxel and not Luka also: “Kind of ridiculous.” pic.twitter.com/SM87XvVY9Y — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) October 22, 2026 Kerr, who has steered the Warriors to four titles, added that guarding Doncic was “not an easy way to start your career,” although he claimed that the six-time All-NBA got off easily during his verbal spat with Lendeborg. “He (Doncic) kind of lured him (Lendeborg) in a little bit. I thought the single technical was kind of ridiculous. They were jawing at each other. I think it was the words Yaxel chose that got him the T, but then Luka made a half-court shot and got in his face. That should be a tech. Should’ve been a double tech. That feels good, the rookie treatment,” said Kerr with a chuckle. The Warriors will battle the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday. Related: Warriors’ Draymond Green weighs in on Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic flare-up Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

item.title: Jamie Carragher tears into ‘disgraceful’ Bruno Fernandes over Man United captain’s Como outburst
item.description: Jamie Carragher has labelled Bruno Fernandes ’ comments on Michael Carrick ’s tactics as “disgraceful” after Manchester United descended into crisis after a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. Cesc Fabregas’ side swept past Carrick’s United with Fernandes visibly upset on the pitch before an outburst at his side’s inability to press. “It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them,” Fernandes said. “But sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.” Th 32-year-old then made a pointed remark that United should have “more brave under pressure,” with the heavy defeat now leaving them 20th in the table after three rounds of fixtures in the league phase and seven games without a win in all competitions. “For Bruno Fernandes to do that, it's a disgrace,” Carragher said on CBS Sports . “When you think about last season, he got player of the year. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick. Bruno Fernandes claimed United should have been braver against Como (Reuters) “Carrick put him back in his rightful position. And he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. “But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent. But in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all. And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off. “When he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. “I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it.”

item.title: How Houston Rockets implemented preseason talking points to great success in opening night romp
item.description: Kevin Durant and the Rockets had 29 fast-break points in Wednesday's season-opening win over the Mavericks as Fred VanVleet's return helped unlock a faster-paced offense. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The two generals, one on the court and the other on the field, faced each other, with one readying for the other's verdict. The former, Fred VanVleet, had just hurled an off-balance pass from his own 3-point line to the opposite end of the court - hitting Kevin Durant in stride for an open dunk. Houston 's point guard turned to his right where the city's quarterback, C.J. Stroud , sat courtside. VanVleet - tilting his hand from side to side - wanted a rating. Stroud gave him two thumbs up. "That's my guy. I don't expect anything less," VanVleet said after the Rockets' 128-110 win at Toyota Center . "I would have been hurt if he would have (given) me a thumbs down." The bucket counted for two of the Rockets' 29 fast-break points - tying their second-highest total from last season, early proof of the faster pace coach Ime Udoka has emphasized through training camp. The Rockets were the second-slowest team in the league last season, forcing them to attack set defenses and often leading to contested shots as the shot clock dwindled. But Wednesday's season opener looked different. Houston shot 52.2% from the field, 44.4% from 3-point range and had assists on 32 of their 47 made baskets. It's just one game against a bad team, but VanVleet's return, offseason additions and a change in tempo gave the Rockets offense some much-needed WD-40 to smoothen the offense. "The ball respects energy and it's contagious," VanVleet said. "So when it's moving and guys are moving and flowing, the shots get better quality and the shots tend to go in more." Playing faster isn't a costless endeavor. Udoka pointed to turnovers and some poor early shot selection as potential tradeoffs. But the Rockets, with VanVleet back on the court and helping limit giveaways, feel they can live with those issues because of the advantages faster pace gets them. Going against a scrambling defense can lead to easy buckets or mismatches as defenders mark whoever is in front of them. Durant and center Alperen Sengun both profited off those "cross-matches." Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) puts up a shot around Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington (25) during the first half at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Houston fueled much of that transition attack with another stylistic shift: Aggressive off-ball defense forcing turnovers. Rather than stay on their assignments, especially when guarding below-average shooters, Rockets defenders would move to the middle of the floor to clog driving and passing lanes. Udoka talked about forcing turnovers as a way to "squeeze" more out of an already-elite defense that allowed the fourth-fewest points per 100 possessions last season, per Cleaning the Glass. It's just one game against a bad team, but VanVleet's return, offseason additions and a change in tempo gave the Rockets offense some much-needed WD-40 to smoothen the offense. "The ball respects energy and it's contagious," VanVleet said. "So when it's moving and guys are moving and flowing, the shots get better quality and the shots tend to go in more." Playing faster isn't a costless endeavor. Udoka pointed to turnovers and some poor early shot selection as potential tradeoffs. But the Rockets, with VanVleet back on the court and helping limit giveaways, feel they can live with those issues because of the advantages faster pace gets them. Going against a scrambling defense can lead to easy buckets or mismatches as defenders mark whoever is in front of them. Durant and center Alperen Sengun both profited off those "cross-matches." Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) puts up a shot around Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington (25) during the first half at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Houston fueled much of that transition attack with another stylistic shift: Aggressive off-ball defense forcing turnovers. Rather than stay on their assignments, especially when guarding below-average shooters, Rockets defenders would move to the middle of the floor to clog driving and passing lanes. Udoka talked about forcing turnovers as a way to "squeeze" more out of an already-elite defense that allowed the fourth-fewest points per 100 possessions last season, per Cleaning the Glass. The Rockets forced turnovers at a bottom-10 rate last season. On Wednesday, the Mavericks committed 21 giveaways that led to 32 Houston points. Houston also entered the season wanting to take more 3-pointers after doing so at one of the lowest rates in the league last season. The Rockets took 36 on Thursday, not an elite mark but still higher than last season's average. The additional shooting opens up opportunities inside. "Last year we started in our backcourt, Twin (Amen Thompson) and Josh Okogie. And a lot of times those guys (were) being left (open) at the 3-point line," Durant said. " … When we got Fred and Marcus Smart out there, who can keep the defense honest at the 3-point line and then twin just roaming around just doing everything … that (puts) everybody in a good position. I think that settled everybody into what they do best." It isn't just about having more shooters. It's also about where they lurk. Jabari Smith Jr., who made four 3-pointers and tied Durant for the team high with 30 points, pointed to Houston's improved off-ball movement, a focus during training camp. The goal, Smith Jr. said, is to keep the defense moving as much as possible. The Rockets were able to implement that change and others to great success in the opener. Now, Houston's goal shifts to maintaining those growth areas moving forward, especially with an imposing test against Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs looming on Friday in Austin.
