item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic isn’t just settling into life with the Los Angeles Lakers ; he is fully embracing the spotlight as the new face of the iconic franchise. Following a dominant 127-105 season-opening victory over the Golden State Warriors, the Slovenian superstar reflected on what it means to carry the mantle for one of the most storied brands in professional sports. Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg tried poking the bear with some second-quarter chatter, but Doncic quickly turned the noise into motivation. He took over the game, pouring in 23 of his 28 points in the first half to put the contest out of reach early. By the end of the night, Doncic stuffed the box score with 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, and three steals in just 30 minutes of action. He was efficient from distance as well, drilling five 3-pointers and dictating the tempo from start to finish. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When asked after the game about carrying the weight of the franchise on his shoulders and his long-term future in Southern California, Doncic kept it real about how much the opportunity means to him. “Obviously it’s the Lakers, it’s one of the biggest organizations in the world, if not the biggest,” Doncic said. “It’s a lot of honor just to be the face of this franchise. I hope I can stay here long. It doesn’t feel different, but like I said, it’s very much an honor, and I’m just enjoying this moment.” Luka on being the face of the Lakers: "Obviously it's the Lakers, it's one of the biggest organizations in the world, if not the biggest. It's a lot of honor just to be the face of this franchise. I hope I can stay here long. It doesn't feel different, but like I said, it's very… pic.twitter.com/rkZvhqqRJS — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 22, 2026 Doncic showed no signs of feeling pressure on opening night. Instead, he delivered the kind of commanding performance that defines elite franchise pillars. If Wednesday’s masterpiece against Golden State was a glimpse of what is to come, purple and gold faithful can rest easy knowing the future of the organization is in capable hands. Doncic is not merely occupying the throne in Los Angeles, he plans on keeping it for a long time. Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

item.title: Celtic v Celta Vigo – This is a must win match for both sides
item.description: Celtic v Celta Vigo – This is a must win match for both sides Tonight is a must win match for both teams so we can expect an open and exciting contest. A draw is pretty much useless for both teams as both need the three points to kickstart their campaign… Callum Osmand of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Some Celtic supporters see the Europa League as a mere distraction, especially with our main rivals for the title spared the distraction of European football, but it’s still a tournament we should aspire to compete in. Tonight’s opponents are La Liga side Celta Vigo who visit Paradise for the first time on competitive business in nearly quarter of a century, and it will be a tough assignment to earn all three points. Benjamin Nygren of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026 . (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) After losing our first two fixtures and conceding seven goals in the process, it’s vital we kickstart our Europa campaign by snatching a victory, which will not only help our hopes of advancing, it will also give us some much needed confidence in our own ability in regards to competing at this level. Celta will also be of similar thinking as much like Celtic they have also lost their opening two fixtures, and will naturally be looking for a positive result. Kieran Tierney of Celtic celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s first goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) There’s also the financial benefit on offer, with £385,000 available for winning all three points, and although not a fortune it’s still a handsome bonus all the same. But the main focus will be to get back to winning ways on the European front, and try to win back some of our dented pride after two disjointed and disappointing performances and terrible results. Celta of course played at Celtic Park back in 2002 during Martin O’Neill’s star studded sides run to Seville, and won 1-0 courtesy of a Henrik Larsson goal which gave the Hoops a slender win to take to Spain. John Hartson of Celtic celebrates scoring during the UEFA Cup, 3rd Round, 2nd leg game between Celta Vigo and Celtic held on December 12, 2002 at the Campo De Futbol De Balaidos in Vigo, Spain. Celta Vigo won the match 2-1, Celtic won the tie 2-2 on away goals. (Photo by Laurence Griffiths/Getty Images) Celtic would unfortunately lose 2-1 in Spain, but would advance on away goals thanks to a John Hartson strike. A repeat of the Celtic Park scoreline would be most welcome tonight as we look to get our first Europa league points on the board. Celtic come into the game with the management team talking up the second half performance in Lisbon last week that was followed by the mauling of Hearts at the weekend with the Bhoys scoring seven times to break the Tynecastle outfit, backed by a small band of Edinburgh’s Shame who thankfully all left early. item.title: Arda Guler jokes about stealing Mbappe’s goal after Real Madrid beat Leipzig: ‘I knew he’d score another’
item.description: Arda Guler jokes about stealing Mbappe’s goal after Real Madrid beat Leipzig: ‘I knew he’d score another’ Arda Guler has revealed why he took the opportunity to score Real Madrid’s second goal in their 4-1 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig , joking that Kylian Mbappe would find the net again anyway. The Turkish midfielder was among Real Madrid’s standout contributors on matchday three and praised his team’s performance both in possession and without the ball. With the European fixture behind them, Guler also made clear that Real Madrid are already focused on the challenge of facing Barcelona in El Clasico. Guler praises Real Madrid’s performance against Leipzig Madrid’s victory provided another positive result in their Champions League campaign, with Guler pleased by the team’s work across both phases of the game. Speaking to Real Madrid TV after the final whistle, the midfielder stressed that the performance was about more than the goals scored. Arda Guler joked about Kylian Mbappe’s goal. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “We’re really pleased because I think we played brilliantly, both with and without the ball. I think we put in a great performance and we’re very happy,” he began. Guler also explained the expectations that come with representing the Spanish giants, insisting that winning must remain the standard regardless of the opponent or competition. “This is what we have to do. We’re Real Madrid, and we have to win every match.” Guler jokes about taking Mbappe’s goal One of the lighter moments from Guler’s interview came when he discussed his goal against Leipzig. The midfielder acknowledged that he had taken the opportunity away from Mbappe, but suggested there was little reason for concern given the French forward’s scoring ability. Arda Guler was crucial for Real Madrid in the Leipzig win. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “I stole the goal from Mbappe, but that’s because I knew he’d score another one. So, no problem.” The young Turk also pointed to the influence of playing at the Santiago Bernabeu, where the home crowd provides an additional motivation for the team. “It’s a key factor because when we play at home, in front of our fans, we try to give it our all for them.” Attention now turns to Sunday’s El Clasico , with Guler recognising the importance of the meeting and promising that Madrid will be ready to compete for the victory. “It’s a big match, a top-class fixture, and we’ll give it our all to win. We’re ready,” he concluded.

item.title: Mbappe and Arda Guler send strong message to Barcelona ahead of El Clasico: ‘We’ll give everything’
item.description: Mbappe and Arda Guler send strong message to Barcelona ahead of El Clasico: ‘We’ll give everything’ Real Madrid stars Kylian Mbappe and Arda Guler have turned their attention to Sunday’s El Clasico against Barcelona. After securing a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Champions League, both players have stressed the importance of the encounter as Jose Mourinho’s side look to reduce the six-point gap in La Liga . Speaking after Madrid’s Champions League fixture against RB Leipzig, Mbappe explained how the squad had deliberately avoided distractions before the European encounter. Mbappe explains Real Madrid’s approach to El Clasico As quoted by FCB World , Mbappe acknowledged that facing Barça carries a different significance from other fixtures. “El Clasico is completely different,” the French forward said. “We were only thinking about the Leipzig match. As for what will happen on Sunday, we can think about it now.” Mbappe is confident of his team putting on a show against Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Mbappe insisted that the squad had not allowed the upcoming Clasico to influence its preparations for Leipzig. “Before that, the team wasn’t thinking about Sunday’s match.” It is the kind of mentality Mourinho always insists on: players should focus on what lies immediately ahead of them. As a manager, he may be forced to consider the Barcelona fixture when making changes to the line-up, but the players cannot afford to get distracted. Arda Guler confident Madrid can challenge Barcelona Guler was equally clear about Madrid’s intentions when asked about the Barcelona encounter. “It’s a big match, a match of the highest level, and we’ll give everything we have to win,” the Turkey midfielder declared. He also emphasised the expectations that come with representing Real Madrid. “We are Real Madrid, and we have to win every match. We’re ready.” For Barcelona, it is a clear message that Los Blancos are completely focussed on the Barça clash and want to give it their best possible effort. Arda Guler has sent a strong message to Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Madrid cannot afford to fall further behind in the title race, particularly with Flick’s side already enjoying a six-point advantage. The Catalan club need to ensure they do exactly that. Barça should put on a statement performance on Sunday to effectively send a message to the rest of La Liga . A victory would extend their lead to nine points and deliver a significant psychological boost after the disappointment against PSG . Sunday’s clash promises to be exciting for both Barça and Madrid fans, and it remains to be seen how the game turns out.

After securing a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Champions League, both players have stressed the importance of the encounter as Jose Mourinho’s side look to reduce the six-point gap in La Liga . Speaking after Madrid’s Champions League fixture against RB Leipzig, Mbappe explained how the squad had deliberately avoided distractions before the European encounter. Mbappe explains Real Madrid’s approach to El Clasico As quoted by FCB World , Mbappe acknowledged that facing Barça carries a different significance from other fixtures. “El Clasico is completely different,” the French forward said. “We were only thinking about the Leipzig match. As for what will happen on Sunday, we can think about it now.” Mbappe is confident of his team putting on a show against Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Mbappe insisted that the squad had not allowed the upcoming Clasico to influence its preparations for Leipzig. “Before that, the team wasn’t thinking about Sunday’s match.” It is the kind of mentality Mourinho always insists on: players should focus on what lies immediately ahead of them. As a manager, he may be forced to consider the Barcelona fixture when making changes to the line-up, but the players cannot afford to get distracted. Arda Guler confident Madrid can challenge Barcelona Guler was equally clear about Madrid’s intentions when asked about the Barcelona encounter. “It’s a big match, a match of the highest level, and we’ll give everything we have to win,” the Turkey midfielder declared. He also emphasised the expectations that come with representing Real Madrid. “We are Real Madrid, and we have to win every match. We’re ready.” For Barcelona, it is a clear message that Los Blancos are completely focussed on the Barça clash and want to give it their best possible effort. Arda Guler has sent a strong message to Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Madrid cannot afford to fall further behind in the title race, particularly with Flick’s side already enjoying a six-point advantage. The Catalan club need to ensure they do exactly that. Barça should put on a statement performance on Sunday to effectively send a message to the rest of La Liga . A victory would extend their lead to nine points and deliver a significant psychological boost after the disappointment against PSG . Sunday’s clash promises to be exciting for both Barça and Madrid fans, and it remains to be seen how the game turns out.

item.title: Bayern Munich interested in Kone for January
item.description: Bayern Munich interested in Kone for January Manu Koné is one of the most important players in Gasperini’s Roma. Born in 2001, he is a pillar of the midfield: alongside Cristante, he forms a well-matched duo that combines balance and dynamism. In the final hours of the summer transfer window, Chelsea attempted to convince the Giallorossi to sell the former Borussia Mönchengladbach player, but the Roman club immediately closed the deal. Koné remains one of the Roma players attracting the most interest from the European big clubs. Koné has attracted the attention of Bayern Munich. According to Calciomercato.it, the Bavarian club is particularly interested in the 2001-born player, so much so that they’re attempting to land him as early as the next winter transfer window. For Gian Piero Gasperini and Roma, the player is unsellable, a crucial asset to maintain the balance of a team that is performing exceptionally well. The only way to change this scenario is with a monstrous offer from Bayern Munich.

item.title: San Francisco Giants Advised To Move on From Struggling Veteran
item.description: The San Francisco Giants have a lot of work to do on the roster. According to one columnist, trading Matt Chapman should be a priority? (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty As the San Francisco Giants look ahead to the offseason, should they prioritize moving on from some of their higher-priced players? One columnist says that should be the team’s top priority, with one player in particular singled out. Matt Chapman Labeled as ‘Most Preferable’ Player to Trade Bleacher Report’s Kerry Miller identified each team’s “most likely” trade in the upcoming offseason. Miller named several of San Francisco’s highest-paid players but singled out third baseman Matt Chapman as the one the team should most prioritize. “The Giants still owe Rafael Devers $211M for seven more seasons, Willy Adames $140M for five more seasons, Matt Chapman $100M for four more seasons and Jung Hoo Lee $63M for three more seasons (if he doesn’t opt out of his final two years next winter),” Miller wrote. “Getting out from under at least one of those contracts—Chapman’s would arguably be most preferable—is going to be the offseason goal for a team that has made the postseason just once in the past decade.” The next question is: how plausible would it be to move on from Chapman? Trading Chapman Would Be Easier Said Than Done It’s easy to see why moving on would be considered a priority. That said, several factors complicate things. The biggest possible roadblock is Chapman’s no-trade clause. If Chapman, a California native who has played most of his career in the Bay Area, doesn’t want to be traded, he won’t be. With a full no-trade clause, Chapman would have to sign off on any deal. The same is true for Willy Adames, as well . But even if the Giants can convince Chapman to sign off on a trade, the rest of his contract complicates matters. Chapman is owed more than $25 million a year through the 2030 season. And while that’s a reasonable contract for a top-tier player, Chapman has not been that for the last two seasons. Chapman made a strong first impression in his first year with the Giants. He posted a .247/.328/.463 slash line, hit 27 home runs, had a 7.1 bWAR, won a Gold Glove and finished 11th in National League MVP voting in 2024. The last two seasons, though, have been a much different story. Over the 2025 and 2026 seasons , Chapman slashed .233/.334/.405, hit a combined 28 home runs and missed a total of 112 games. The 2026 season was a particular struggle. Injuries limited Chapman to only 86 games. In that time, he slashed at just .235/.324/.368, adding only 7 home runs. Plenty of teams will pay $25 million for an MVP candidate. But convincing a team to take on a declining player in his mid-30s who’s owed $25 million over each of the next four seasons? That wouldn’t be easy for the Giants. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post San Francisco Giants Advised To Move on From Struggling Veteran appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Verstappen could take a different strategic route in Austin thanks to Pirelli’s tyre selection
item.description: After two consecutive Grand Prix victories, Max Verstappen heads to Austin, where he will face a significant challenge. According to tyre supplier Pirelli, tyre wear could play a major role at the United States Grand Prix. A revised tyre selection does, however, give Red Bull Racing an additional strategic option. Pirelli is bringing three types of dry-weather tyres: the C2 hard, the C3 medium and the C4 soft. As is well known, softer tyres generally offer more grip, but tend not to last as long. Teams must therefore weigh up whether to prioritise speed or run longer without changing tyres. The change this weekend concerns the hard tyre. Last year, Pirelli used the harder C1 for this compound, but this time, it is the C2. The medium and soft tyres remain the same as in 2025, narrowing the gap between the three available compounds. Why the tyres will be under strain in Austin The Circuit of the Americas puts stress on both the front and rear tyres. In the first sector, fast corners come in quick succession, repeatedly forcing the front tyres to steer the car in a different direction. Later in the lap, the rear tyres have to do much of the work as drivers accelerate out of slow corners. This can cause them to overheat and lose grip. The asphalt also plays a part. The section between Turns 9 and 11 has been resurfaced, while the rest of the track surface is getting older. Pirelli expects tyre wear to be a significant factor as a result. Last year, several tyres were heavily worn by the end of their stints. For the drivers, this means that pushing flat out at all times is not necessarily the fastest way to complete the race. Those who ask too much of their tyres early on may lose grip later and start posting progressively slower lap times. They may also need to make an extra pit stop. New tyre selection gives Verstappen an opportunity Pirelli expects a one-stop strategy to be the most likely option. The C2 could play an important role, as it should be capable of completing many consecutive laps. High temperatures could change that plan, however: if the tyres lose performance more quickly, alternative strategies become more appealing. Can Max Verstappen repeat his successful 2025 weekend in Austin? - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Can Max Verstappen repeat his successful 2025 weekend in Austin? - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool A second tyre change costs time, but also provides fresh rubber. Red Bull will therefore have to judge whether Verstappen can make up enough time on new tyres to offset the extra stop. High temperatures could change that plan, however: if the tyres lose performance more quickly, alternative strategies become more appealing. Can Max Verstappen repeat his successful 2025 weekend in Austin? - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Can Max Verstappen repeat his successful 2025 weekend in Austin? - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool A second tyre change costs time, but also provides fresh rubber. Red Bull will therefore have to judge whether Verstappen can make up enough time on new tyres to offset the extra stop. Staying out longer only makes sense as long as his lap times do not drop off too sharply. Last year, Verstappen won in Austin with a one-stop strategy. He started on medium tyres and switched to softs on lap 33. He made it to the end of the race on them, although he had to manage his tyres carefully towards the finish. This shows that opting for a relatively soft tyre can work, but it is no guarantee for this weekend. Red Bull's focus returns to the long runs Longer runs during the practice sessions will therefore naturally be important. Drivers complete multiple consecutive laps on the same set of tyres during these runs. This allows Red Bull to assess how much speed Verstappen loses over time and how long he can safely stay out. After all, a single fast lap says little about how long a tyre will last. Verstappen's chances of securing a third consecutive Grand Prix victory in Austin will also depend on how well the RB22 can maintain its pace over a longer run of laps.

item.title: Another Man Utd meltdown! Matheus Cunha & Michael Carrick caught in FURIOUS off-camera row as Champions League disaster sparks dressing room revolt
item.description: Manchester United’s season has plunged into further chaos following a humiliating Champions League defeat that saw internal tensions boil over. Reports have emerged of a heated confrontation between head coach Michael Carrick and forward Matheus Cunha as the Red Devils' winless run continues to haunt Old Trafford. Tensions boil over in Italy The crisis enveloping Manchester United deepened significantly on Wednesday night following a heavy 4-1 away loss to Como. Cesc Fabregas' side dismantled their English visitors in the Champions League, extending United's dismal winless streak to seven matches. Nico Paz orchestrated the rout with a memorable brace, scoring his first inside two minutes to instantly deflate the travelling support. While the result itself was disastrous, touchline developments have sparked even greater concern. According to The Sun' s Samuel Luckhurst , Carrick was involved in a 'relatively robust' altercation with Cunha that television cameras missed. Fans also picked up on the palpable friction between the Brazilian forward and his manager during a chaotic first-half display in Italy. Half-time changes highlight rift The tension between Cunha and Carrick culminated in immediate tactical changes at the interval. The head coach ruthlessly withdrew the Brazilian forward at half-time, introducing Amad Diallo in a desperate bid to inject life into his struggling side. Carlos Baleba was also brought on as United attempted to salvage any pride from the wreckage. These sweeping alterations ultimately proved ineffective. Just four minutes into the second period, Anastasios Douvikas capitalised on further defensive fragility to trigger a relentless wave of attacks from the hosts. Paz soon added his second following a glaring United error, punishing a visiting side that looked completely disjointed and bereft of ideas. The off-camera clash serves as a stark indicator of the rapidly deteriorating atmosphere behind the scenes. With United outplayed in every department, the frustrated exchanges on the touchline highlight a squad fracturing under immense pressure just two months into the campaign. FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Fernandes questions tactical approach The Cunha altercation is merely the latest sign of a broader dressing room revolt. Just a week after Lisandro Martinez publicly slammed the club's hierarchy over a lack of squad reinforcements following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, Bruno Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s game plan . The Portuguese midfielder expressed clear frustration over the coaching staff's decision to avoid a man-to-man press, claiming it allowed Como to build early confidence. "It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early," the United captain told reporters. "Conceding early makes us go into [the] game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation." Tensions boil over in Italy The crisis enveloping Manchester United deepened significantly on Wednesday night following a heavy 4-1 away loss to Como. Cesc Fabregas' side dismantled their English visitors in the Champions League, extending United's dismal winless streak to seven matches. Nico Paz orchestrated the rout with a memorable brace, scoring his first inside two minutes to instantly deflate the travelling support. While the result itself was disastrous, touchline developments have sparked even greater concern. According to The Sun' s Samuel Luckhurst , Carrick was involved in a 'relatively robust' altercation with Cunha that television cameras missed. Fans also picked up on the palpable friction between the Brazilian forward and his manager during a chaotic first-half display in Italy. Half-time changes highlight rift The tension between Cunha and Carrick culminated in immediate tactical changes at the interval. The head coach ruthlessly withdrew the Brazilian forward at half-time, introducing Amad Diallo in a desperate bid to inject life into his struggling side. Carlos Baleba was also brought on as United attempted to salvage any pride from the wreckage. These sweeping alterations ultimately proved ineffective. Just four minutes into the second period, Anastasios Douvikas capitalised on further defensive fragility to trigger a relentless wave of attacks from the hosts. Paz soon added his second following a glaring United error, punishing a visiting side that looked completely disjointed and bereft of ideas. The off-camera clash serves as a stark indicator of the rapidly deteriorating atmosphere behind the scenes. With United outplayed in every department, the frustrated exchanges on the touchline highlight a squad fracturing under immense pressure just two months into the campaign. FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Fernandes questions tactical approach The Cunha altercation is merely the latest sign of a broader dressing room revolt. Just a week after Lisandro Martinez publicly slammed the club's hierarchy over a lack of squad reinforcements following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, Bruno Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s game plan . The Portuguese midfielder expressed clear frustration over the coaching staff's decision to avoid a man-to-man press, claiming it allowed Como to build early confidence. "It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early," the United captain told reporters. "Conceding early makes us go into [the] game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation." Carrick swiftly fired back, aiming pointed criticism at his players' work ethic rather than the tactical setup. The 45-year-old labelled the squad's application as unacceptable, bluntly stating: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win." Carrick fighting to save his job FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Manchester United now find themselves navigating a full-blown crisis both on and off the pitch. With seven consecutive matches without a victory, Carrick faces immense pressure to bridge the growing divide within his squad and restore basic defensive discipline. The glaring lack of on-field effort, compounded by public player dissent, leaves the Old Trafford hierarchy with critical decisions to make. The Red Devils must urgently find a way to halt this alarming slide, or they risk their entire season unravelling before the busy winter schedule even begins.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard Reacts to His 1st Game Back With Raptors
item.description: Kawhi Leonard Raptors Getty Toronto Raptors superstar Kawhi Leonard reacted to his first game back in Toronto after seven years away with the Los Angeles Clippers. Leonard spent one season in Toronto in 2018-19, and it was a memorable one, as he helped lead the Raptors to the franchise’s first and only NBA Championship. Immediately after winning the chip, Leonard signed a free-agent contract to head back home to Los Angeles and play with the Clippers, where he spent seven seasons, achieving very little playoff success in the process. With the Clippers moving to a rebuilding phase, it made sense to move on from Leonard, especially in the wake of the Aspiration scandal, and Los Angeles traded him back to Toronto this summer. Kawhi Leonard and Raptors Win Against Chicago Bulls On Wednesday night, the Raptors won their season opener at home with a dominant 135-92 victory over the Chicago Bulls . Leonard scored 23 points in 24 minutes of game action in the blowout win. After the game, the always-stoic Leonard spoke to reporters and shared his reaction to a successful return to Toronto. “I’m not really assessing it right now. I never really do. We won the game. Just trying to do what it takes. It’s one game. We’re going to get better. That’s it,” Leonard said. Kawhi Leonard on how he would assess his performance tonight: “I’m not really assessing it right now. I never really do.” “We won the game. Just trying to do what it takes.” “It’s one game. We’re going to get better. That’s it.” pic.twitter.com/T1w4fzeyep — Omer Osman (@OmerOsman200) October 22, 2026 Kawhi Leonard Explains Why He Wanted to Stay on the Floor The Raptors completely blew out the Bulls, so Raptors coach Darko Rajakovic could have easily just sat Leonard on the bench the entire second half had he wanted to do some load management. But Leonard wanted to play and get some minutes in despite the game being out of reach. “I haven’t got a chance to play much in training camp. Any minutes I could get, or continue to play. I know we was blowing them out, but the goal was to try to get 23-24 minutes tonight. I need more reps to learn plays. This is where you get better… You can’t wait till practice and shoot 100 shots. You need game reps. Even on the defensive end, just being able to make calls on the fly instinctively,” Leonard said. Kawhi Leonard on why he wanted to be back on the floor: “I haven’t got a chance to play much in training camp. Any minutes I could get, or continue to play.” “I know we was blowing them out, but the goal was to try to get 23-24 minutes tonight. I need more reps to learn plays.”… https://t.co/bgE77vFbpV pic.twitter.com/dSIcxA7DE5 — Omer Osman (@OmerOsman200) October 22, 2026 This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Kawhi Leonard Reacts to His 1st Game Back With Raptors appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: JD Vance seemingly ignored by slew of Cincinnati Bengals players
item.description: A number of Cincinnati Bengals players walked past Vice President J.D. Vance largely without interacting with him on Wednesday when he visited the team’s practice facility with his son. Vance, an Ohio native and longstanding Bengals fan, made the visit before a midterms campaign rally in support of Republican candidates including Vivek Ramaswamy, who is in a tight battle in the state’s gubernatorial race. In a video posted on X, most of the players were seen filing past Vance without engaging. However, tight end Drew Sample was seen shaking hands and exchanging words with the vice president. JD Vance greets Bengals players on the way out pic.twitter.com/lMKvYRpMfE — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 Responding to the clip, the singer-songwriter Bill Madden wrote on X: “This is what TOTAL HUMILIATION looks like: JD Vance attempted to greet Cincinnati Bengals players in the locker room and got snubbed and ghosted by every single player except one.” Dov Kleiman, a NFL commentator, also said: “The Bengals are under heavy criticism online for IGNORING Vice President JD Vance as he tried to greet them. The large majority of the team did not shake his hand or even acknowledge Vance.” Newsweek contacted Vance via the White House press office, and the Cincinnati Bengals’ press office for comment via email outside of regular office hours. Vice President JD Vance speaking at a campaign rally in Sharonville, Ohio, on Wednesday. This is a developing story. More to follow. item.title: Continuing To Improve The Cleveland Browns Heading Towards 2027 - Offensive Review
item.description: theOBR While I regularly write about next season and roster predictions, this looks more at what the team is likely to do. In this piece I want to focus on where the Browns need to improve to get to above average in each position room for 2027. It will focus much more on the starters rather than seeing anything in terms of depth. They have a fantastic amount of cash and draft picks at their disposal to keep adding more to this young talented roster. Quarterback The arguments can continue of if Deshaun Watson is good enough to be a bridge quarterback in 2027 or not, when it comes to winning consistently, it doesn't really matter. Bridge quarterbacks and players you find in free agency, aren't going to take you to the Super Bowl in a loaded AFC. I don't see them going the route of trading multiple picks for a player after how it went previously. So that means the plan will be to take a quarterback next season in the draft. April is far too far away to worry about where the Browns will pick and who the best quarterbacks will be. The season is more about working out if Watson can be the bridge than anything else. Running Back At running back it feels like they need a second back to pair with Judkins in a 1A and 1B scenario like when they had Chubb and Hunt previously. They have plenty of change of pace backs to chose from between Sampson, Sanders and potentially McLaughlin. Luckily it is possible to pick up the type of backs they need in free agency at a relatively decent price. Wide Receiver After years of struggling to get quality at the position, they have three starting quality receivers. They will either need to keep Jeudy next season or add another via free agency, trade or the draft. I would keep Jeudy and then focus on adding more in the draft on day three with the hope you can develop someone. Tight End They need to find more at tight end. While Fannin has plenty of promise he has the potential to be Kyle Pitts type player who can be a massive part of the passing offense but low value in the run game. While they could focus on chasing a run blocking tight end, it will be limiting to have a clear run blocker and a clear pass catcher. This gives a tell to the opposition each time one is on the field. They would be better suited looking to add a more all-around tight end. Even if this effectively moves Fannin to being a hybrid tight end/wide receiver alongside a new tight end, Boston and Concepcion. Offensive Line Everything has been looking very positive on the offensive line over the last few weeks. While people questioned Howard, he has really turned it around and is looking like the $21m a year tackle they traded for. There is a very real chance they run it back in 2027 when it comes to their starters. With four of the starters likely locked in, it is just a question of does Elgton Jenkins return in 2027 or not. As things stand it would be likely but there is a long season to go and he will turn 31 towards the end of the calendar year. Coac

Quarterback The arguments can continue of if Deshaun Watson is good enough to be a bridge quarterback in 2027 or not, when it comes to winning consistently, it doesn't really matter. Bridge quarterbacks and players you find in free agency, aren't going to take you to the Super Bowl in a loaded AFC. I don't see them going the route of trading multiple picks for a player after how it went previously. So that means the plan will be to take a quarterback next season in the draft. April is far too far away to worry about where the Browns will pick and who the best quarterbacks will be. The season is more about working out if Watson can be the bridge than anything else. Running Back At running back it feels like they need a second back to pair with Judkins in a 1A and 1B scenario like when they had Chubb and Hunt previously. They have plenty of change of pace backs to chose from between Sampson, Sanders and potentially McLaughlin. Luckily it is possible to pick up the type of backs they need in free agency at a relatively decent price. Wide Receiver After years of struggling to get quality at the position, they have three starting quality receivers. They will either need to keep Jeudy next season or add another via free agency, trade or the draft. I would keep Jeudy and then focus on adding more in the draft on day three with the hope you can develop someone. Tight End They need to find more at tight end. While Fannin has plenty of promise he has the potential to be Kyle Pitts type player who can be a massive part of the passing offense but low value in the run game. While they could focus on chasing a run blocking tight end, it will be limiting to have a clear run blocker and a clear pass catcher. This gives a tell to the opposition each time one is on the field. They would be better suited looking to add a more all-around tight end. Even if this effectively moves Fannin to being a hybrid tight end/wide receiver alongside a new tight end, Boston and Concepcion. Offensive Line Everything has been looking very positive on the offensive line over the last few weeks. While people questioned Howard, he has really turned it around and is looking like the $21m a year tackle they traded for. There is a very real chance they run it back in 2027 when it comes to their starters. With four of the starters likely locked in, it is just a question of does Elgton Jenkins return in 2027 or not. As things stand it would be likely but there is a long season to go and he will turn 31 towards the end of the calendar year. Coaching When it comes to the offensive coaching staff, they need to focus on fixing the run game. It was semi working during the Ravens game, but this feels more like a one off than fixing it at this stage. It will be interesting to see if they can do anything over the next few weeks, but after the bye week could be the most telling spell. Conclusion Considering the starting shopping list for the offensive side of the ball currently sits at drafting a quarterback, a free agency running back and adding a tight end that can block, it isn't too extreme. Hitting on the quarterback will always be incredibly hard as teams have proven they haven't found a decent way to judge which college quarterbacks will and won't be successful. If they can fix this run game it could be a top offense in the league if they can make the right selection. It is why coming into this season I was incredibly high on the Browns in 2027 and I see no reason to pause the optimism.

item.title: ‘Wasn’t a top pick’-Super Bowl champion explains why Shedeur Sanders has struggled at Browns
item.description: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images Three-time Super Bowl champion Willie McGinest has explained why Shedeur Sanders has struggled to establish himself as the Cleveland Browns’ starting quarterback, arguing that the young signal-caller did not arrive in the NFL with the same pressure as a top draft pick. Sanders has spent much of the current season watching from the sidelines as Deshaun Watson leads Cleveland under head coach Todd Monken. The Browns have made a strong start with Watson at the helm, leaving Sanders facing questions about his future and growing speculation over a potential trade. Willie McGinest says Shedeur Sanders must prove himself on the field McGinest believes Sanders’ draft position played a role in the expectations placed on him when he entered the league. Speaking about the Browns quarterback, the former New England Patriots linebacker said: “Shedeur didn’t put the pressure on the position by coming into the league. I mean that by saying he wasn’t like a top pick. Now, if you’re a number one pick, if you’re a top 10 pick, then you put the pressure on the position right away.” McGinest pointed to Russell Wilson as an example of a later-round pick who quickly forced his way into the starting conversation with the Seattle Seahawks. He argued that Sanders had not yet produced the same evidence to convince Cleveland that he deserved the job. “I know there’s a lot of hype and it’s the hype behind the name or the lineage where you come from or what you are actually doing on the football field. At some point, if he’s doing what he needs to do on the football field, he’ll get an opportunity,” McGinest added. Sanders did start eight games for Cleveland last season after Dillon Gabriel suffered a concussion, throwing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. His tendency to hold the ball for too long was also a concern, with his average time to throw reaching 3.24 seconds from his debut in Week 11, the highest figure in the NFL over that period. Watson has since strengthened his position as Cleveland’s starter, helping the Browns build a 4-2 record across their first six games. Sanders has also signed with Young Money APAA Sports for representation, a move that has fuelled speculation about his future. However, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones suggested a trade before the deadline would still be a surprise. Sanders now needs to make the most of his opportunities if he is to change the Browns’ thinking about his role. item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic welcomes Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg to NBA: ‘Talking crazy’
item.description: There’s a common idiom that most NBA players follow when it comes to the league’s best players: Don’t poke the bear. But when it came to Luka Doncic on Wednesday night during the Lakers’ season-opening blowout win over the Warriors at Crypto.com Arena, Yaxel Lendeborg not only poked the bear , but ignited a barrage of chirping late in the second quarter. And the Slovenian superstar made it clear that whatever the Warriors rookie said was out of bounds. Yaxel Lendeborg defends Luka Doncic during the Lakers’ 127-105 season-opening win over the Warriors on Oct. 21, 2026 in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images “He was talking crazy,” Doncic said. The trash talk started when the Lakers 6-foot-8 guard picked up a shooting foul against Lendeborg late in the second, with Doncic laughing as the No. 11 pick in June’s NBA draft became frustrated with the call. Luka Doncic drives past Yaxel Lendeborg during the first half of the Lakers’ season-opening blowout victory over the Warriors. Getty Images Even after Lendeborg subbed out, Doncic kept talking to the 6-foot-9 forward out of Michigan while he was on the bench after knocking down a fadeaway against Will Richard, and once again while Sandro Mamukelashvili was shooting free throws. Lendeborg picked up a technical foul with 22 seconds left in the first half after he and Doncic, presumably, kept chirping at each other. The punctuation mark to the jawing came right before halftime, when Doncic nailed a buzzer-beating halfcourt shot to give the Lakers a 66-52 lead going into the game’s break. "He was talking crazy" – Luka Doncic on the chirping with Yaxel Lendeborg. Says he's trying not to pick up as many technical fouls and refrained from picking one up tonight. https://t.co/sYqydObQt7 pic.twitter.com/1azX8moQAx — Khobi Price (@khobi_price) October 22, 2026 “Nobody understands what he says,” Austin Reaves quipped of Doncic. “He’s not speaking English. I didn’t understand anything and barely knew anything was going on. So, I know we need an article to come out and I’m going to start paying people to talk s— to him so gets [into] another gear when people start trying to talk to him.” The most impressive part of the back-and-forth was Doncic not picking up a technical foul during the whole ordeal after being assessed 16 technical fouls last season. Luka Doncic and Yaxel Lendeborg look on during a break in the action in the Lakers’ season-opening blowout win over the Warriors. NBAE via Getty Images “I wasn’t trying to talk back this season,” Doncic said. “I’m trying to not get techs. So it was the first time that [it] was not a double tech, because I didn’t say nothing. So I’m working on it. But as you see, it worked great.”

item.title: New Mexico State leans on James Jones, defense to outlast Sam Houston, 30-24
item.description: New Mexico State celebrates after 30-24 win over Sam Houston on October 22, 2026 | Steve Helwick Sam Houston had a chance to defend its home turf in a standalone Wednesday night Weekday CUSA matchup. Instead, New Mexico State left Huntsville with a long-awaited breakthrough. Behind a career-best performance from running back James Jones and a suffocating defensive effort, the Aggies defeated the Bearkats 30-24 at Bowers Stadium, securing their first road victory of the 2026 season. “We did a good job coming out and getting the first victory of the season,” New Mexico State head coach Tony Sanchez said. “I thought our guys played a good game, played a good four-quarter game, and it was really good to see at the end, with four minutes left, them kicking the ball deep and us being able to just run the clock out. Proud of our guys and happy for them.” The star of the night was Jones, who continued to lead the CUSA in rushing. The New Mexico State running back recorded his fourth 100-yard game of 2026 and shattered his career-high with 178 yards. He also opened the Aggies’ scoring in the second quarter with his lone touchdown of the night. “It’s a blessing,” Jones said of his performance. “I thank the Lord for every opportunity that He gave me. I appreciate what He’s given me. And my o-line, I can’t do it without them. Them up front fighting, our defense getting stops, we’re all playing together. It isn’t even on me, it’s up front.” Jones saved his best work for the final minutes. Clinging to a 6-point lead, New Mexico State leaned on its star running back to drain the final 4:00 of clock and deny the Bearkats an opportunity at a comeback victory. Jones gained 39 yards on four carries during the final drive, converting a 4th-and-2 with 29 seconds remaining to seal the Aggies’ first one-score victory since November 2025. “The final four minutes, I told my coach — Coach (David) Yost does a great job calling plays — but I was telling him, ‘I need the ball in my hands. I’m gonna ice it,’” Jones said. “Then the o-line was doing their thing up front, and then I popped one. That’s what got us in that situation — the o-line up front.” Despite the victory, New Mexico State’s offense had to overcome a pair of costly mistakes early in the game. Roughly two minutes into the contest, the Aggies fell behind 7-0 when Sam Houston wide receiver Terrence Guillory II blocked a punt and Railyn Adams recovered the loose ball in the end zone. Then in the second quarter, New Mexico State’s incomplete lateral pass in its own territory was ruled a fumble, and the Bearkats cashed in with a field goal. item.content:encoded: New Mexico State celebrates after 30-24 win over Sam Houston on October 22, 2026 | Steve Helwick Sam Houston had a chance to defend its home turf in a standalone Wednesday night Weekday CUSA matchup. Instead, New Mexico State left Huntsville with a long-awaited breakthrough. Behind a career-best performance from running back James Jones and a suffocating defensive effort, the Aggies defeated the Bearkats 30-24 at Bowers Stadium, securing their first road victory of the 2026 season. “We did a good job coming out and getting the first victory of the season,” New Mexico State head coach Tony Sanchez said. “I thought our guys played a good game, played a good four-quarter game, and it was really good to see at the end, with four minutes left, them kicking the ball deep and us being able to just run the clock out. Proud of our guys and happy for them.” The star of the night was Jones, who continued to lead the CUSA in rushing. The New Mexico State running back recorded his fourth 100-yard game of 2026 and shattered his career-high with 178 yards. He also opened the Aggies’ scoring in the second quarter with his lone touchdown of the night. “It’s a blessing,” Jones said of his performance. “I thank the Lord for every opportunity that He gave me. I appreciate what He’s given me. And my o-line, I can’t do it without them. Them up front fighting, our defense getting stops, we’re all playing together. It isn’t even on me, it’s up front.” Jones saved his best work for the final minutes. Clinging to a 6-point lead, New Mexico State leaned on its star running back to drain the final 4:00 of clock and deny the Bearkats an opportunity at a comeback victory. Jones gained 39 yards on four carries during the final drive, converting a 4th-and-2 with 29 seconds remaining to seal the Aggies’ first one-score victory since November 2025. “The final four minutes, I told my coach — Coach (David) Yost does a great job calling plays — but I was telling him, ‘I need the ball in my hands. I’m gonna ice it,’” Jones said. “Then the o-line was doing their thing up front, and then I popped one. That’s what got us in that situation — the o-line up front.” Despite the victory, New Mexico State’s offense had to overcome a pair of costly mistakes early in the game. Roughly two minutes into the contest, the Aggies fell behind 7-0 when Sam Houston wide receiver Terrence Guillory II blocked a punt and Railyn Adams recovered the loose ball in the end zone. Then in the second quarter, New Mexico State’s incomplete lateral pass in its own territory was ruled a fumble, and the Bearkats cashed in with a field goal. New Mexico State’s defense ensured those miscues did not prove costly. The Aggies allowed just 13 yards in the first half, surrendering 20 in the opening quarter before holding Sam Houston to -7 yards in the second. The Bearkats finished with just nine first downs and 11 rushing yards, repeatedly struggling to win at the line of scrimmage. “I thought our defense played lights out,” Sanchez said. “Other than that very first snap of the second half, the guys did a fantastic job of creating pressure on the quarterback all night. We got some important turnovers and they did a really good job.” Sanchez also credited his offense for its response, and New Mexico State captured its first lead in the final seconds of the first half on a 2-play, 43-yard touchdown drive that consumed just 18 seconds. “Offensively, it was really good to see us put that touchdown on the board before halftime and come out early in the second half and get another touchdown,” Sanchez said. The Aggies’ defense came up with two crucial turnovers, each setting up a short field that led to a touchdown. In the second quarter, Josiah Charles intercepted Sam Houston quarterback Landyn Locke and returned the ball to the 1-yard line, setting up Jones’ touchdown. Late in the third quarter, Kaian Roberts-Day blew up a flea-flicker in the backfield and recovered the fumble, setting up TJ Washington Jr. for a rushing touchdown. “We’ve lost the turnover battle three weeks in a row,” said Sanchez, whose team was a minus-5 in turnover margin prior to Wednesday. “It’s really gotten in the way. You go all the way back to the Hawaii game, obviously the UNM game, the FIU game, and we weren’t winning the turnover battle. We had one really bad turnover at the end, but to win the turnover battle tonight made a big difference in the game.” Sam Houston’s offense finally found the explosive play it desperately needed to open the second half. After leaving the game in the second quarter with a leg injury, Locke returned to action and connected with Tim Burns Jr. for an 81-yard touchdown on the first snap after halftime, handing the Bearkats a 17-14 lead. Locke’s longest pass since Week 2 ended the team’s 12-quarter drought without an offensive touchdown, dating back to Sept. 26. Locke was briefly replaced by true freshman backup Brett Holloway before finishing the game with 235 passing yards. Sam Houston head coach Phil Longo explained the injury situation postgame. “They thought it was a fibula fracture, and they X-ray’d him, and you’re looking at losing your starting quarterback for the year,” Longo said. “Then 20 minutes goes by and no fracture, and they tape him up, we’re gonna treat him, and he comes back out and he couldn’t really move laterally, so we held him out for a little bit. We ran him around the sideline to see if he could move enough to do the things he needs to do. When he proved to me that he could do that and the trainers gave me the okay, we put him back on the field. For playing hurt, he actually played fairly decent in the second half.” The Bearkats’ momentum after Locke’s touchdown pass was brief. New Mexico State responded three minutes later with a touchdown strike from Adam Damante to AJ Williams III. The touchdown sparked a 16-0 run that put the Aggies back in control. It wasn’t Williams’ only highlight Wednesday night. The 6’4” wide receiver had an additional contested catch in the end zone, finishing the night with two touchdowns — both which handed New Mexico State the lead. “AJ has been waiting on this,” Jones said. “I’m very happy for him that everybody got to see what he can do, because he’s been doing it in practice all year.” Sam Houston eventually responded cutting the deficit to 30-24 with an MJ Dowdy rushing touchdown with four minutes remaining. But the Bearkats could not regain possession, as Jones and the Aggies’ offensive line dominated the final series. “I thought we challenged them from a heart and emotional and a grind standpoint in the second half, and they responded,” Longo said. “But too little, too late, obviously, so that’s kinda how the game went. We responded, played more physical, played with some more emotion and some passion offensively in the second half but came up short because it wasn’t enough.” Longo also commented on Sam Houston’s recurring offensive struggles in a night they were outgained by the visitor 203-11 on the ground. “I didn’t see yardage, that’s for sure,” Longo said on the offensive performance. “We addressed a lot of the issues we’d had the past two weeks. I think a lot of people understand we’re struggling up front because of some injuries. You gotta plug in the next guy and you gotta go. We even tried to redirect our plan this week, just to try and play maybe to the strengths of some of the guys we have in. But we just lack continuity up front right now, and it’s affecting us offensively.” Sam Houston (1-6, 0-3 CUSA) remains winless against FBS competition this season and has fallen to 3-16 in the Longo era. The Bearkats are on the brink of missing bowl eligibility for the second consecutive season, and to preserve those hopes, they must respond on the road Tuesday at Missouri State. “There’s a sense of urgency from the get-go,” Longo said. “I want for us to manage some of the issues we’re having on offense and fix them. item.title: Steve Kerr Gives Terrible Warriors Update For Stephen Curry Fans
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr speaks to Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors during the first half of their preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on October 06, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty One of the biggest topics about the Golden State Warriors this season is about whether they’d make a big trade. More help is needed for Stephen Curry to have any chance of contending for another NBA Championship with this Warriors core. Jimmy Butler will miss the start of the season with his injury recovery to see minimal help behind Curry on the flawed roster. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr shut down any chance of Golden State risking their future to help Curry: “Do we throw away our entire future to build around a 39-year-old Steph? He turns 39 in March, right? Does it make sense now to throw away all those picks? Hell no,. Our fan base might have been thrilled if we had traded five firsts and two of our better players for one of the big fish. They might have been happy for a year, and they might have been miserable for the next decade if it backfired.” Kerr’s blunt comment upsets Curry fans who believe the Warriors owe it to him to add more star power. Curry helped lead the Warriors to relevance after years of struggles before his arrival. Most Golden State fans hold immense loyalty to Curry, Draymond Green, and Klay Thompson for changing the culture. Will The Warriors Make Any Moves To Help Stephen Curry? The situation in Golden State is dire with a terrible opening night performances against the Los Angeles Lakers . It is hard to see this roster competing for a playoff spot in the loaded Western Conference with talented teams trying to make the play-in. Curry needs help with the news of Kristaps Porzingis being ruled out indefinitely with an unknown illness. The Warriors kept most of the same roster from last season to see the same issues returning and frustrating the fan base. Anthony Davis and Trey Murphy are the most common names linked to Golden State. Unfortunately, Kerr’s comment about not trading future picks or young prospects likely blocks both moves. Opposing teams want real talent, and the Warriors are not looking to give up anything of value to increase their chances of winning now. Could Stephen Curry Want To Leave Warriors? The next question for such a quote focuses on what Curry feels about it. Most quotes from Curry confirms he wants to retire with the Warriors as a rare one franchise superstar. However, the lack of moves could mean he’s retiring in irrelevance if they don’t change course. It is hard to see this roster competing for a playoff spot in the loaded Western Conference with talented teams trying to make the play-in. Curry needs help with the news of Kristaps Porzingis being ruled out indefinitely with an unknown illness. The Warriors kept most of the same roster from last season to see the same issues returning and frustrating the fan base. Anthony Davis and Trey Murphy are the most common names linked to Golden State. Unfortunately, Kerr’s comment about not trading future picks or young prospects likely blocks both moves. Opposing teams want real talent, and the Warriors are not looking to give up anything of value to increase their chances of winning now. Could Stephen Curry Want To Leave Warriors? The next question for such a quote focuses on what Curry feels about it. Most quotes from Curry confirms he wants to retire with the Warriors as a rare one franchise superstar. However, the lack of moves could mean he’s retiring in irrelevance if they don’t change course. Next season will see Golden State holding a lot of cap space with Green and Butler entering free agency. It appears the Warriors would rather pay a free agent rather than trade assets to get better faster. The Washington Wizards could let Davis walk if he wants too much money. Curry could opt to force his way out via a trade demand, but the odds are against that. Even in a losing scenario, Curry’s reputation and legacy matter more in Golden State than on a new contender. Don’t expect him to follow peers like LeBron James and Kevin Durant to start team hopping this late. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Steve Kerr Gives Terrible Warriors Update For Stephen Curry Fans appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: The Wayward Train: My Dad’s Notre Dame Thanksgiving Adventure in 1963
item.description: An unforgettable Thanksgiving, a football game at Yankee Stadium, and a train ride that took an unexpected detour through Canada. Since Notre Dame has a bye week, I thought we’d take this week’s Throwback Thursday a little off the rails. Literally. Instead of revisiting a memorable victory or one of those classic Notre Dame football games that still makes us smile, I’m sharing a story from my dad’s college days. It’s a story that involves Thanksgiving on Long Island, a football game at Yankee Stadium, one of the most difficult moments in American history, and a train ride home that turned into an international adventure. Oh, and there’s a photograph of my dad sleeping upside down in his train seat. Yes, you read that correctly. But before we get to the train, we need to go back to Thanksgiving 1963. A Thanksgiving Invitation My dad was a student at Notre Dame when his classmate Mike Fiore invited him and a few friends to spend Thanksgiving with his family on Long Island. The plan was to enjoy the holiday with Mike’s family, explore a little of New York, and attend Notre Dame’s Thanksgiving Day football game against Syracuse at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Mike was studying civil engineering at Notre Dame, following in the footsteps of his father, who was also a Notre Dame graduate. My dad remembers Mike’s father as a highly accomplished civil engineer who had worked on bridge projects. The Fiore family welcomed the young men into their home for the Thanksgiving holiday, treating them to a wonderful dinner and giving them the opportunity to explore Long Island and New York City during their visit. They arrived Wednesday evening, attended the Notre Dame–Syracuse game at Yankee Stadium on Thanksgiving morning, and spent the rest of the holiday weekend enjoying time with friends before heading back to South Bend on Sunday. For a group of college students, it sounded like a pretty terrific Thanksgiving getaway. But the timing made this particular holiday unlike any other. On November 22, 1963, just six days before Notre Dame and Syracuse would meet at Yankee Stadium, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas. When I asked my dad what he remembered about that Thanksgiving, he told me the country was still very much in shock. It’s difficult to imagine what those days must have felt like for a group of young college students. They were away from campus, spending time with friends, and looking forward to a football game, but the entire nation was grieving. item.content:encoded: An unforgettable Thanksgiving, a football game at Yankee Stadium, and a train ride that took an unexpected detour through Canada. Since Notre Dame has a bye week, I thought we’d take this week’s Throwback Thursday a little off the rails. Literally. Instead of revisiting a memorable victory or one of those classic Notre Dame football games that still makes us smile, I’m sharing a story from my dad’s college days. It’s a story that involves Thanksgiving on Long Island, a football game at Yankee Stadium, one of the most difficult moments in American history, and a train ride home that turned into an international adventure. Oh, and there’s a photograph of my dad sleeping upside down in his train seat. Yes, you read that correctly. But before we get to the train, we need to go back to Thanksgiving 1963. A Thanksgiving Invitation My dad was a student at Notre Dame when his classmate Mike Fiore invited him and a few friends to spend Thanksgiving with his family on Long Island. The plan was to enjoy the holiday with Mike’s family, explore a little of New York, and attend Notre Dame’s Thanksgiving Day football game against Syracuse at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Mike was studying civil engineering at Notre Dame, following in the footsteps of his father, who was also a Notre Dame graduate. My dad remembers Mike’s father as a highly accomplished civil engineer who had worked on bridge projects. The Fiore family welcomed the young men into their home for the Thanksgiving holiday, treating them to a wonderful dinner and giving them the opportunity to explore Long Island and New York City during their visit. They arrived Wednesday evening, attended the Notre Dame–Syracuse game at Yankee Stadium on Thanksgiving morning, and spent the rest of the holiday weekend enjoying time with friends before heading back to South Bend on Sunday. For a group of college students, it sounded like a pretty terrific Thanksgiving getaway. But the timing made this particular holiday unlike any other. On November 22, 1963, just six days before Notre Dame and Syracuse would meet at Yankee Stadium, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas. When I asked my dad what he remembered about that Thanksgiving, he told me the country was still very much in shock. It’s difficult to imagine what those days must have felt like for a group of young college students. They were away from campus, spending time with friends, and looking forward to a football game, but the entire nation was grieving. And Notre Dame’s football team had experienced that historic week in a particularly unusual way. A Football Season Overshadowed by History In 2018, Notre Dame published a fascinating retrospective titled “Yankee Stadium, Circa 1963,” written by Matt Storin, who had served as the senior manager of the 1963 Fighting Irish football team. Storin, a member of Notre Dame’s Class of 1964 who went on to a distinguished journalism career, offered a firsthand look at a difficult season and an unforgettable Thanksgiving week. Notre Dame had been scheduled to face Iowa on November 23, the day after Kennedy’s assassination. According to Storin, the Irish had already arrived in Iowa City and settled into their hotel when the game was canceled. The team returned to South Bend on Sunday morning, only to turn around and travel to New York on Wednesday for its Thanksgiving matchup with Syracuse. The Irish were struggling through a season in which victories had been hard to come by. Under interim head coach Hugh Devore, Notre Dame had won just two of its first eight games. There was also uncertainty beyond the football field. Storin recalled the economic anxiety surrounding South Bend as Studebaker announced plans to end automobile production in the city. Between the assassination, the struggling football program, and concerns about the local economy, it was a particularly difficult time for the Notre Dame community. Yet the football season continued. Storin remembered the team arriving in New York and checking into the Waldorf Astoria. The traveling squad numbered fewer than 40 players, and the players had little time to prepare once they reached the city. The Thanksgiving Day game would kick off at 10:30 in the morning, an unusual start time by today’s standards, before a crowd of 56,672 at the original Yankee Stadium. For Storin, walking through the third-base dugout and onto the famous playing field was an unforgettable experience. For my dad and his friends, it was another chance to cheer on the Irish. Unfortunately, the game itself would provide yet another frustrating chapter in Notre Dame’s 1963 season. Notre Dame vs. Syracuse: A Familiar Ending The 1963 Notre Dame Football Review described Yankee Stadium as an unusual setting for college football. The enormous grandstands towered above the players, casting long shadows across the field and blocking much of the late-November sunlight. The Irish had experienced several heartbreaking losses that season, and the Syracuse game would follow a painfully familiar pattern. Syracuse controlled much of the early action but repeatedly failed to capitalize on scoring opportunities. On one promising drive, Orange running back Jim Nance fumbled near the Notre Dame goal line, and Tom Longo recovered for the Irish. Eventually, Syracuse broke through when Wally Mahle connected with Billy Hunter on a six-yard touchdown pass. Dick Arrington blocked the extra-point attempt, leaving Notre Dame trailing 6-0. Late in the second quarter, the Irish finally found some offensive momentum. Starting at their own 14-yard line, Notre Dame put together an impressive 86-yard scoring drive. Nick Rassas gained 20 yards around right end, Jim Kelly hauled in a 15-yard pass from Sandy Bonvechio, and Tommy MacDonald helped move the Irish deep into Syracuse territory. Then Notre Dame reached into its bag of tricks. Bonvechio pitched the ball to halfback Frank Budka, who threw a touchdown pass to MacDonald in the end zone. Ken Ivan added the extra point, giving Notre Dame a 7-6 lead with just one minute remaining in the first half. For a team that had struggled so much throughout the season, perhaps this would finally be the afternoon when everything came together. The Irish defense certainly did its part. Bill Pfeiffer intercepted a Syracuse pass in the third quarter, and MacDonald added another interception to his impressive career total. Bob Lehmann and Ken Maglicic also helped thwart Syracuse scoring opportunities as the Irish clung to their narrow lead. But the fourth quarter brought another heartbreaking finish. With 3:28 remaining, Syracuse quarterback Rich King connected with Mike Koski for the go-ahead touchdown. A successful two-point conversion extended the Orange lead to 14-7. Notre Dame couldn’t answer, and the Irish fell to Syracuse by seven points. In his 2018 recollection, Storin described the loss as the fourth time that season Notre Dame had surrendered a game-deciding score late in the contest. He also remembered an exchange with a Syracuse player after the game. The player sympathized with Notre Dame’s difficult afternoon, and Storin replied that it had been much like the rest of the season. Sometimes, that’s just the way football goes. One interesting detail from Storin’s account is that Notre Dame wore green jerseys that Thanksgiving Day. The Irish wouldn’t wear green again until the famous 1977 game against USC. And although nobody knew it at the time, the 1963 season was about to become an important turning point in Notre Dame football history. Just 18 days after the Syracuse game, Notre Dame announced that Northwestern head coach Ara Parseghian would take over the program. The Irish would go from a 2-7 season in 1963 to a 9-1 record in 1964, narrowly missing a national championship. But back on Thanksgiving weekend in 1963, none of that was known. item.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
item.description: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...
